controlled-rectifiers-firing-angle-and-a.application: Power Electronics: DC motor drives and battery chargers with phase-controlled front ends.
controlled-rectifiers-firing-angle-and-a.meaning: Controlled Rectifiers: Firing Angle and Average Output: Delaying each thyristor's turn-on by the firing angle chops the waveform's front and lowers the average output predictably - the cosine law of phase control.
controlled-rectifiers-firing-angle-and-a.name: Average output of a full-wave controlled rectifier

convection-newtons-law-of-cooling-and-th.application: Heat & Mass Transfer: Sizing heatsinks, radiators and condenser air-side surfaces.
convection-newtons-law-of-cooling-and-th.meaning: Convection: Newton's Law of Cooling and the Nusselt Number: Convective heat flow is a coefficient times area times temperature difference - and the Nusselt number reports how much the moving fluid multiplies plain conduction.
convection-newtons-law-of-cooling-and-th.name: Newton cooling and Nusselt number

cooling-load-and-sensible-heat-ratio.application: Refrigeration & Air Conditioning: Selecting coils and apparatus dew points that match the space SHR line.
cooling-load-and-sensible-heat-ratio.meaning: Cooling Load and Sensible Heat Ratio: A space's cooling duty splits into temperature-changing sensible load and moisture-removing latent load, and their ratio must match the coil's own ratio or comfort fails.
cooling-load-and-sensible-heat-ratio.name: Sensible load and SHR

cooling-time-and-its-share-of-the-mouldi.application: Polymer Science & Processing: Setting cycle time expectations when quoting a moulding job.
cooling-time-and-its-share-of-the-mouldi.meaning: Cooling Time and Its Share of the Moulding Cycle: Injection moulding cycle time is dominated by cooling, and cooling time grows with the square of wall thickness - which is why thin walls are cheap and thick ones are not.
cooling-time-and-its-share-of-the-mouldi.name: Cooling time for a plate of thickness 2s

corrosion-cells-and-cathodic-protection.application: Engineering Chemistry: Galvanizing steel and hanging sacrificial anodes on ship hulls.
corrosion-cells-and-cathodic-protection.meaning: Corrosion Cells and Cathodic Protection: Corrosion is a short-circuited electrochemical cell: the more active metal becomes the anode and dissolves, and protection works by forcing that role onto a cheaper metal.
corrosion-cells-and-cathodic-protection.name: Corrosion cell driving potential

counters-ripple-versus-synchronous-and-m.application: Digital Electronics: Frequency division and event counting where intermediate states must never be read (synchronous).
counters-ripple-versus-synchronous-and-m.meaning: Counters: Ripple versus Synchronous and Modulus Design: A counter is flip-flops plus steering logic; ripple counters pay delay per stage while synchronous counters pay it once - and the modulus decides how many stages are needed.
counters-ripple-versus-synchronous-and-m.name: Stage count and worst-case delay

counting-permutations-combinations-and-p.application: Discrete Mathematics: Sizing test suites: how many input pairs must be covered.
counting-permutations-combinations-and-p.meaning: Counting: Permutations, Combinations and Pigeonhole: Order matters in permutations and not in combinations, and the pigeonhole principle turns any surplus of items over boxes into a guaranteed collision.
counting-permutations-combinations-and-p.name: Counting rules

coupling-metrics-and-the-dependency-poin.application: Object Oriented Programming: Architecture tests that fail the build when a stable package imports a volatile one.
coupling-metrics-and-the-dependency-poin.meaning: Coupling Metrics and the Dependency-Pointing Rule: Package level coupling can be measured and then governed: a package's instability is the share of its dependencies that point outward, and stable packages are the ones that must be abstract.
coupling-metrics-and-the-dependency-poin.name: Instability and distance from the main sequence

creep-shrinkage-and-durability-cover.application: Concrete Technology: Deflection and camber prediction for slabs and long-span beams.
creep-shrinkage-and-durability-cover.meaning: Creep, Shrinkage and Durability Cover: Concrete keeps deforming long after it hardens - creep under load, shrinkage as it dries - and the cover depth decides how long the reinforcement survives the environment.
creep-shrinkage-and-durability-cover.name: Creep coefficient and total strain

critical-path-method-and-project-float.application: Operations Research & Optimization: Construction and product-launch schedules where liquidated damages ride on the completion date.
critical-path-method-and-project-float.meaning: Critical Path Method and Project Float: A project's duration is its longest dependency chain, and every activity off that chain carries float - slack that scheduling software hides and schedulers must manage.
critical-path-method-and-project-float.name: Forward/backward pass and float

cstr-volume-for-a-second-order-reaction-.application: Chemical Reaction Engineering: Sizing stirred reactors for liquid-phase reactions where mixing and temperature control matter more than plug flow.
cstr-volume-for-a-second-order-reaction-.meaning: CSTR Volume for a Second-Order Reaction and the Cost of High Conversion: A well-mixed reactor always runs at the lowest concentration in the system, so the volume needed to reach high conversion with second-order kinetics grows very steeply.
cstr-volume-for-a-second-order-reaction-.name: CSTR volume for second-order kinetics with equal-molar feed

cut-off-grade-and-break-even-economics.application: Mine Planning & Operations: Reporting ore reserves and deciding what material reports to the mill versus the waste dump.
cut-off-grade-and-break-even-economics.meaning: Cut-Off Grade and Break-Even Economics: The grade at which a tonne of ore pays for its own mining and processing is a single equation, and it moves with the metal price - which is why reserves are re-reported whenever prices change.
cut-off-grade-and-break-even-economics.name: Break-even cut-off grade

cutting-speed-in-turning-operations.application: Workshop Practice: Selecting a safe lathe spindle speed.
cutting-speed-in-turning-operations.meaning: Cutting Speed in Turning Operations: Cutting speed is the tangential speed of the work surface at the cutting edge and sets the spindle-speed relationship.
cutting-speed-in-turning-operations.name: Turning cutting speed

cyclomatic-complexity-and-basis-path-tes.application: Software Engineering: Setting a minimum test count for safety-critical code reviews (DO-178C style branch coverage).
cyclomatic-complexity-and-basis-path-tes.meaning: Cyclomatic Complexity and Basis Path Testing: The number of independent paths through a routine is a small integer you can compute from its flow graph - and it is the minimum count of tests that can claim to have exercised its logic.
cyclomatic-complexity-and-basis-path-tes.name: McCabe's cyclomatic number

darcy-flow-through-a-porous-reservoir.application: Reservoir Engineering: Core-flow tests and reservoir deliverability estimates.
darcy-flow-through-a-porous-reservoir.meaning: Darcy Flow Through a Porous Reservoir: Darcy's law relates single-phase flow through a porous medium to permeability, area, pressure gradient, and viscosity.
darcy-flow-through-a-porous-reservoir.name: One-dimensional Darcy flux

darcy-weisbach-friction-loss-in-pipe-flo.application: Fluid Mechanics: Sizing pump heads for plant piping networks and building services.
darcy-weisbach-friction-loss-in-pipe-flo.meaning: Darcy-Weisbach Friction Loss in Pipe Flow: Head loss along a pipe is a dimensionless friction factor times a velocity head, scaled by how much pipe the flow traverses - the workhorse of every piping calculation.
darcy-weisbach-friction-loss-in-pipe-flo.name: Darcy-Weisbach equation

datums-and-feature-control-frames-in-gd-.application: Engineering Drawing & CAD: Accepting or rejecting machined parts on CMM inspection reports.
datums-and-feature-control-frames-in-gd-.meaning: Datums and Feature Control Frames in GD&T: Geometric tolerancing controls shape and location relative to named datums, and material-condition modifiers let a feature earn extra tolerance when it is made smaller or larger than its worst case.
datums-and-feature-control-frames-in-gd-.name: Bonus tolerance at MMC

dc-machine-speed-back-emf-and-field-weak.application: Electrical Machines I: Predicting the droop of a DC drive as load increases.
dc-machine-speed-back-emf-and-field-weak.meaning: DC Machine Speed, Back EMF and Field Weakening: A DC machine's speed follows its back-EMF law: at fixed field, speed falls with armature drop, and weakening the field raises speed at the cost of torque.
dc-machine-speed-back-emf-and-field-weak.name: Back EMF and speed

decimal-reduction-time-in-thermal-preser.application: Food Process Engineering & Safety: Understanding thermal preservation targets.
decimal-reduction-time-in-thermal-preser.meaning: Decimal Reduction Time in Thermal Preservation: The decimal reduction time D is the exposure time at a specified temperature needed for a one-log reduction of a target organism.
decimal-reduction-time-in-thermal-preser.name: Log-linear survival model

defect-removal-efficiency-and-release-re.application: Software Engineering: Release-gate criteria that state a DRE target alongside coverage and defect-density thresholds.
defect-removal-efficiency-and-release-re.meaning: Defect Removal Efficiency and Release Readiness: Release readiness is a ratio, not a feeling: the share of defects found before release, and the sample size needed to reach a target.
defect-removal-efficiency-and-release-re.name: Defect removal efficiency

defibrillator-energy-delivery-and-transt.application: Biomedical Instrumentation & Devices: Protocol energy selection (escalating or fixed per waveform type) in resuscitation.
defibrillator-energy-delivery-and-transt.meaning: Defibrillator Energy Delivery and Transthoracic Impedance: A defibrillator dumps a controlled joule-count through the chest, and the current that actually reaches the heart depends on energy, waveform and the patient's transthoracic impedance.
defibrillator-energy-delivery-and-transt.name: Stored energy and delivered current

degrees-paths-and-euler-circuits-in-grap.application: Discrete Mathematics: Route planning that must traverse every street once (snow ploughing, meter reading, link inspection).
degrees-paths-and-euler-circuits-in-grap.meaning: Degrees, Paths and Euler Circuits in Graphs: Every edge contributes two degrees, so degree sums count edges twice - and that simple parity fact decides when a graph can be drawn in one continuous stroke.
degrees-paths-and-euler-circuits-in-grap.name: Handshaking lemma and Euler criterion

development-length-and-anchorage-of-rein.application: Design of Reinforced Concrete Structures: Detailing beam and column reinforcement so that bars are anchored where moment is high.
development-length-and-anchorage-of-rein.meaning: Development Length and Anchorage of Reinforcement: A bar must be embedded long enough for the bond between steel and concrete to develop the force in it, and that length scales with bar diameter and stress.
development-length-and-anchorage-of-rein.name: Development length from bond stress

dft-and-fft-compute-cost.application: Digital Signal Processing: Real-time audio, OFDM subcarrier demodulation and motor-vibration diagnostics.
dft-and-fft-compute-cost.meaning: DFT and FFT Compute Cost: The DFT's direct evaluation costs N^2 operations while the FFT reuses symmetry to cost N log N - a difference that decides what real-time signal processing is possible.
dft-and-fft-compute-cost.name: Complexity contrast

diffie-hellman-key-exchange-and-forward-.application: Cryptography & Network Security: TLS session-key agreement, where ephemeral DH/ECDH provides forward secrecy by default in modern profiles.
diffie-hellman-key-exchange-and-forward-.meaning: Diffie-Hellman Key Exchange and Forward Secrecy: Two parties can agree on a secret over a public channel because exponentiation is easy while discrete logarithms are not - and ephemeral keys turn that agreement into forward secrecy.
diffie-hellman-key-exchange-and-forward-.name: Diffie-Hellman shared secret

diffusion-in-solids-ficks-second-law-and.application: Materials Science & Engineering: Carburizing, nitriding and decarburization control in gear and shaft manufacture.
diffusion-in-solids-ficks-second-law-and.meaning: Diffusion in Solids: Fick's Second Law and Carburizing: Atoms migrate through solids by thermally activated jumps, so diffusion depth grows with the square root of time - the law that sizes every heat-treatment soak.
diffusion-in-solids-ficks-second-law-and.name: Diffusion length and Fick's second law

diode-bias-and-series-current.application: Basic Electronics: Rectifiers, indicator LEDs, and input protection.
diode-bias-and-series-current.meaning: Diode Bias and Series Current: A forward-biased diode conducts while a resistor limits current; the source voltage is shared by both.
diode-bias-and-series-current.name: Series current with a constant-drop diode

diode-i-v-behaviour-and-load-line-checks.application: Electronic Devices & Circuits: Rectifiers, clamps, and transistor junction bias.
diode-i-v-behaviour-and-load-line-checks.meaning: Diode I–V Behaviour and Load-Line Checks: A diode's current changes nonlinearly with junction voltage; a series resistor and source establish the operating point.
diode-i-v-behaviour-and-load-line-checks.name: Series load-line approximation

distance-vector-routing-and-count-to-inf.application: Computer Networks: Understanding RIP's 15-hop limit as a loop-breaker, not a topology opinion.
distance-vector-routing-and-count-to-inf.meaning: Distance-Vector Routing and Count-to-Infinity: Routers believing only their neighbours' rumours can trap a stale path in a two-node loop that climbs one hop-cost at a time toward infinity.
distance-vector-routing-and-count-to-inf.name: Bellman-Ford update

distillation-mccabe-thiele-stages-and-re.application: Mass Transfer Operations: Designing and debottlenecking binary columns: stage count, feed stage and reflux policy.
distillation-mccabe-thiele-stages-and-re.meaning: Distillation: McCabe-Thiele Stages and Reflux Ratio: A distillation column is a staircase between an equilibrium curve and two operating lines, and the reflux ratio sets both the staircase's shape and the column's energy bill.
distillation-mccabe-thiele-stages-and-re.name: Rectifying operating line

divergence-curl-and-the-integral-theorem.application: Engineering Mathematics III: Converting Gauss-law integrals in electrostatics into enclosed-charge counts.
divergence-curl-and-the-integral-theorem.meaning: Divergence, Curl, and the Integral Theorems: Divergence measures outward flux density and curl measures local rotation, and the integral theorems let you swap a hard surface or line integral for an easier volume or area one.
divergence-curl-and-the-integral-theorem.name: Divergence theorem

double-slit-interference-and-fringe-spac.application: Engineering Physics: Measuring unknown wavelengths with a simple optical bench.
double-slit-interference-and-fringe-spac.meaning: Double-Slit Interference and Fringe Spacing: Overlapping waves from two narrow slits add or cancel by path difference, producing bright fringes whose spacing measures the wavelength.
double-slit-interference-and-fringe-spac.name: Fringe spacing

drag-force-and-terminal-velocity.application: Fluid Mechanics: Parachute and re-entry decelerator sizing.
drag-force-and-terminal-velocity.meaning: Drag Force and Terminal Velocity: A body moving through fluid pays a force proportional to velocity squared, and free fall ends when that force balances weight - the terminal velocity.
drag-force-and-terminal-velocity.name: Drag and terminal velocity

drilling-cutting-speed-spindle-rpm-and-f.application: Workshop Practice: Setting manual drill presses safely before tapping or reaming.
drilling-cutting-speed-spindle-rpm-and-f.meaning: Drilling: Cutting Speed, Spindle RPM and Feed: The material sets the cutting speed at the edge; the drill diameter converts that speed into the spindle RPM the machine must actually turn.
drilling-cutting-speed-spindle-rpm-and-f.name: Spindle speed from cutting speed

duty-cycling-and-battery-life-estimation.application: Internet of Things Systems Design: Multi-year agricultural, utility-meter and asset-tracking deployments.
duty-cycling-and-battery-life-estimation.meaning: Duty Cycling and Battery Life Estimation: A battery-powered node lives on its average current, not its peak: sleeping microseconds and waking milliseconds blend into one number that sets months or years.
duty-cycling-and-battery-life-estimation.name: Average current and battery life

dynamic-power-in-cmos-logic.application: VLSI Design: Comparing voltage/frequency operating points.
dynamic-power-in-cmos-logic.meaning: Dynamic Power in CMOS Logic: CMOS dynamic power grows with switched capacitance, the square of supply voltage, clock frequency, and activity.
dynamic-power-in-cmos-logic.name: CMOS dynamic power

dynamic-power-voltage-scaling-and-energy.application: VLSI Design: Writing a power budget for a mobile or thermally limited design.
dynamic-power-voltage-scaling-and-energy.latex: P=\alpha C V^2 f,\qquad E_{cycle}=\alpha C V^2
dynamic-power-voltage-scaling-and-energy.meaning: Dynamic Power, Voltage Scaling and Energy per Operation: A digital block's power is activity times capacitance times voltage squared times frequency, which is why voltage scaling is the strongest energy lever available and why it slows the circuit down.
dynamic-power-voltage-scaling-and-energy.name: Dynamic power and switching energy

earthwork-volumes-trapezoidal-and-prismo.application: Estimating & Costing: Highway, canal and site-grading earthwork estimates and payment certificates.
earthwork-volumes-trapezoidal-and-prismo.meaning: Earthwork Volumes: Trapezoidal and Prismoidal Rules: Longitudinal earthwork volumes come from cross-section areas at intervals, and the rule chosen to interpolate between them shifts the answer - and the payment - by several percent.
earthwork-volumes-trapezoidal-and-prismo.name: Trapezoidal and prismoidal formulas

ecg-signal-chain-bandwidth-and-common-mo.application: Biomedical Instrumentation & Devices: Designing and specifying patient monitors, Holter recorders and research ECG front ends.
ecg-signal-chain-bandwidth-and-common-mo.meaning: ECG Signal Chain: Bandwidth and Common-Mode Rejection: An ECG front end must pass a 1 mV, 0.05-150 Hz differential signal sitting on volts of 50 Hz interference picked up by the body - a job for bandwidth discipline and common-mode rejection.
ecg-signal-chain-bandwidth-and-common-mo.name: CMRR interference suppression

economic-dispatch-and-incremental-cost.application: Power Systems: Day-ahead and real-time market clearing prices are system lambdas at scale.
economic-dispatch-and-incremental-cost.meaning: Economic Dispatch and Incremental Cost: The cheapest way to meet a load is to run every online generator at the same incremental cost - equal slopes of the cost curves, not equal outputs.
economic-dispatch-and-incremental-cost.name: Equal-incremental-cost criterion

economic-order-quantity-and-inventory-tr.application: Operations Research & Optimization: Choosing an initial replenishment lot size.
economic-order-quantity-and-inventory-tr.meaning: Economic Order Quantity and Inventory Trade-Off: The basic EOQ model balances fixed ordering cost against inventory holding cost under steady, deterministic demand.
economic-order-quantity-and-inventory-tr.name: Economic order quantity

effective-access-time-and-the-fault-rate.application: Operating Systems: Capacity planning for a system whose resident set is nearly as large as physical memory.
effective-access-time-and-the-fault-rate.meaning: Effective Access Time and the Fault-Rate Budget: The cost of virtual memory is decided by one product: page-fault rate times fault service time, which sets the maximum fault rate a system can tolerate for a given slowdown.
effective-access-time-and-the-fault-rate.name: Effective access time and its fault-rate budget

effort-estimation-function-points-and-co.application: Software Engineering: Sanity-checking vendor bids against an independent size-based estimate.
effort-estimation-function-points-and-co.meaning: Effort Estimation: Function Points and COCOMO: Estimation models trade a size measurement for an effort number, and both classic models agree on one thing: effort grows superlinearly with size.
effort-estimation-function-points-and-co.name: Basic COCOMO (organic mode)

eigenvalues-and-the-characteristic-equat.application: Engineering Mathematics I: Principal-component analysis, where the top eigenvector of a covariance matrix is the direction of most variance.
eigenvalues-and-the-characteristic-equat.meaning: Eigenvalues and the Characteristic Equation: An eigenvector keeps its direction under a linear map, and its eigenvalue is the factor by which the map stretches it; eigenvalues are the roots of a polynomial built from the matrix.
eigenvalues-and-the-characteristic-equat.name: Characteristic equation

emf-equation-of-dc-machines.application: Electrical Machines I: Sizing generators and predicting motor back-EMF for drive design.
emf-equation-of-dc-machines.meaning: EMF Equation of DC Machines: One equation links flux, speed and winding layout to the generated voltage - and the same expression, with current instead of voltage, gives the torque.
emf-equation-of-dc-machines.name: Generated EMF

engine-performance-maps-bsfc-and-the-tor.application: Internal Combustion Engines: Choosing gear ratios and operating points for fuel economy, not just peak power.
engine-performance-maps-bsfc-and-the-tor.meaning: Engine Performance Maps: BSFC and the Torque-Power Curve: Power is torque times speed, but efficiency is brake-specific fuel consumption - and the BSFC map shows the small island where an engine actually earns its fuel.
engine-performance-maps-bsfc-and-the-tor.name: Power and BSFC

equilibrium-and-structural-determinacy.application: Structural Analysis: Finding support reactions before drawing shear and moment diagrams.
equilibrium-and-structural-determinacy.meaning: Equilibrium and Structural Determinacy: A planar structure at rest must satisfy force and moment equilibrium; equilibrium alone does not guarantee stability or code adequacy.
equilibrium-and-structural-determinacy.name: Planar rigid-body equilibrium

equivalent-standard-axles-and-pavement-l.application: Transportation Engineering: Selecting pavement thickness from a design traffic figure.
equivalent-standard-axles-and-pavement-l.meaning: Equivalent Standard Axles and Pavement Load Accumulation: Pavement damage grows roughly with the fourth power of axle load, so one heavy vehicle can be worth thousands of cars and the design traffic is counted in equivalent standard axles.
equivalent-standard-axles-and-pavement-l.name: Equivalent standard axles and cumulative traffic

error-budget-burn-rate-and-two-window-al.application: Site Reliability Engineering: Alerting policies that page on budget consumption rather than on a static error rate.
error-budget-burn-rate-and-two-window-al.meaning: Error-Budget Burn Rate and Two-Window Alerting: A burn rate expresses how fast an error budget is being spent, which turns an SLO into an alerting rule: a short window catches fast burns, a longer window catches slow ones.
error-budget-burn-rate-and-two-window-al.name: Burn rate against an error budget

error-propagation-in-a-derived-measureme.application: Measurements & Instrumentation: Specifying instrument accuracy for a measurement chain before purchase.
error-propagation-in-a-derived-measureme.latex: \left(\frac{\Delta z}{z}\right)^2=\left(\frac{\Delta x}{x}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\Delta y}{y}\right)^2,\qquad \Delta z=\sqrt{(\Delta x)^2+(\Delta y)^2}
error-propagation-in-a-derived-measureme.meaning: Error Propagation in a Derived Measurement: A computed quantity inherits the errors of its inputs, and the size of the inherited error depends on how the inputs are combined - which tells you which instrument to buy next.
error-propagation-in-a-derived-measureme.name: Relative error in a product and in a sum

eutectic-reactions-and-reading-phase-dia.application: Materials Science & Engineering: Choosing solder, casting and bearing alloys by their freezing range.
eutectic-reactions-and-reading-phase-dia.meaning: Eutectic Reactions and Reading Phase Diagrams: A phase diagram is a map of stable phases versus temperature and composition, and the eutectic point is its most important landmark: the lowest-melting composition, where one liquid freezes into two solids at once.
eutectic-reactions-and-reading-phase-dia.name: Eutectic invariant reaction

evaporator-steam-economy-and-multiple-ef.application: Heat Transfer Operations: Concentrating fruit juice, milk, black liquor and brine wherever steam dominates operating cost.
evaporator-steam-economy-and-multiple-ef.meaning: Evaporator Steam Economy and Multiple Effects: Evaporating water costs steam, and multiple-effect evaporation recycles each kilogram's latent heat across stages - the steam economy counts how many times it gets used.
evaporator-steam-economy-and-multiple-ef.name: Steam economy

extrusion-screw-output-and-drag-flow.application: Polymer Science & Processing: Line-rate calculations for pipe, film and profile extrusion.
extrusion-screw-output-and-drag-flow.meaning: Extrusion: Screw Output and Drag Flow: A single-screw extruder is a viscous drag pump: the rotating screw drags melt forward at a rate set by geometry and speed, minus a pressure-driven backflow.
extrusion-screw-output-and-drag-flow.name: Metering-section output

fabric-cover-yarn-spacing-diameter-and-p.application: Textile Fibre & Fabric Engineering: Designing shirting, technical and filtration fabrics to air-permeability targets.
fabric-cover-yarn-spacing-diameter-and-p.meaning: Fabric Cover: Yarn Spacing, Diameter and Permeability: How much of a fabric's area is yarn rather than hole governs its look, hand, air and water behaviour - and cover is computed from yarn diameter against spacing, system by system.
fabric-cover-yarn-spacing-diameter-and-p.name: Cover factor per system and combined area cover

factor-of-safety-and-allowable-stress.application: Machine Design: Sizing shafts, fasteners, gears, and machine frames.
factor-of-safety-and-allowable-stress.meaning: Factor of Safety and Allowable Stress: A factor of safety compares a material or component limit with the design demand under stated failure criteria.
factor-of-safety-and-allowable-stress.name: Factor of safety

fatigue-endurance-limit-and-the-goodman-.application: Machine Design: Sizing axles, springs and fasteners for infinite-life service.
fatigue-endurance-limit-and-the-goodman-.meaning: Fatigue: Endurance Limit and the Goodman Line: Cyclic loads fail parts far below yield; the endurance limit bounds infinite life for fully reversed stress, and the Goodman line extends that bound to mean-stress reality.
fatigue-endurance-limit-and-the-goodman-.name: Goodman relation

ficks-law-and-diffusive-flux.application: Mass Transfer Operations: Sizing absorption, extraction, and membrane transfer.
ficks-law-and-diffusive-flux.meaning: Fick's Law and Diffusive Flux: For one-dimensional molecular diffusion in a simple medium, flux moves down the concentration gradient.
ficks-law-and-diffusive-flux.name: Fick's first law

field-capacity-and-field-efficiency.application: Agricultural Machinery & Irrigation Systems: Sizing machinery for a field-operation window.
field-capacity-and-field-efficiency.meaning: Field Capacity and Field Efficiency: Field efficiency compares measured effective field capacity with theoretical capacity based on implement width and travel speed.
field-capacity-and-field-efficiency.name: Theoretical field capacity

fir-filter-length-from-the-transition-wi.application: Digital Signal Processing: Budgeting real-time filter cost in audio and instrumentation processing.
fir-filter-length-from-the-transition-wi.meaning: FIR Filter Length from the Transition Width: A linear-phase FIR filter's cost is decided by its transition width: halving the width doubles the number of taps, and the tap count is the arithmetic load you must budget for.
fir-filter-length-from-the-transition-wi.name: Tap estimate from transition width and stopband attenuation

fir-versus-iir-filters-stability-and-pha.application: Digital Signal Processing: Audio crossover and communications pulse shaping (FIR, phase-critical).
fir-versus-iir-filters-stability-and-pha.latex: H_{\mathrm{FIR}}(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}b_k z^{-k};\qquad H_{\mathrm{IIR}}(z)=\frac{\sum b_k z^{-k}}{1+\sum a_k z^{-k}};\qquad \tau_{\mathrm{FIR}}=\frac{N-1}{2}
fir-versus-iir-filters-stability-and-pha.meaning: FIR versus IIR Filters: Stability and Phase Trade-Offs: FIR filters buy guaranteed stability and exact linear phase with taps; IIR filters buy sharp cutoffs with poles - and the choice is which property the application cannot lose.
fir-versus-iir-filters-stability-and-pha.name: Transfer structures and linear-phase delay

first-order-batch-reactor-conversion.application: Chemical Reaction Engineering: Estimating batch residence time.
first-order-batch-reactor-conversion.meaning: First-Order Batch-Reactor Conversion: For a constant-volume first-order batch reaction, concentration decays exponentially with elapsed reaction time.
first-order-batch-reactor-conversion.name: First-order conversion

first-order-step-response-and-time-const.application: Control Systems Engineering: Interpreting sensor lag and process response.
first-order-step-response-and-time-const.meaning: First-Order Step Response and Time Constant: A stable first-order system reaches about 63.2% of a step change after one time constant.
first-order-step-response-and-time-const.name: Unit-step response

flexural-resistance-of-a-reinforced-conc.application: Design of Reinforced Concrete Structures: Preliminary flexural checks for beams and slabs.
flexural-resistance-of-a-reinforced-conc.meaning: Flexural Resistance of a Reinforced-Concrete Beam: A singly reinforced beam resists bending through a compression block in concrete and tension carried mainly by steel reinforcement.
flexural-resistance-of-a-reinforced-conc.name: Lever-arm moment resistance (simplified section check)

flip-flop-timing-setup-hold-and-maximum-.application: Digital Logic Design: Static timing analysis sign-off on every FPGA and ASIC design.
flip-flop-timing-setup-hold-and-maximum-.meaning: Flip-Flop Timing: Setup, Hold and Maximum Clock Rate: A flip-flop samples correctly only if data is stable around the clock edge, and those stability windows set the shortest legal clock period of the whole synchronous system.
flip-flop-timing-setup-hold-and-maximum-.name: Timing constraint

flow-measurement-orifice-meters-and-disc.application: Fluid Flow Operations: Custody-transfer and process measurement of liquids, gases and steam with DP transmitters.

mosfet-operating-regions-cut-off-triode-.meaning: MOSFET Operating Regions: Cut-Off, Triode and Saturation: One gate-voltage inequality chain decides whether a MOSFET is an open switch, a voltage-controlled resistor, or a current source - and analog and digital design live in different regions on purpose.
mosfet-operating-regions-cut-off-triode-.name: Region conditions and saturation current

mtbf-mttr-and-steady-state-availability.application: Site Reliability Engineering: Sizing error budgets and on-call staffing from measured MTBF/MTTR.
mtbf-mttr-and-steady-state-availability.meaning: MTBF, MTTR and Steady-State Availability: Availability is the fraction of time a system is up, and it decomposes into how often it fails (MTBF) and how fast you recover (MTTR) - both are engineering targets, not fate.
mtbf-mttr-and-steady-state-availability.name: Availability from failure and repair times

multiplexers-and-decoders-as-combination.application: Digital Logic Design: Data routing inside ALUs and FPGA fabric, where mux trees are the primitive.
multiplexers-and-decoders-as-combination.latex: Y=\sum_{i=0}^{2^{n}-1} m_i\, I_i,\qquad f(x)=\text{mux with } I_i=f(\text{row } i)
multiplexers-and-decoders-as-combination.meaning: Multiplexers and Decoders as Combinational Building Blocks: A 2^n-to-1 multiplexer routes one of 2^n data inputs to the output by an n-bit select, which makes it a lookup table in hardware - and any Boolean function can be wired into its data inputs.
multiplexers-and-decoders-as-combination.name: Multiplexer output and function mapping

myhill-nerode-classes-and-minimal-automa.application: Theory of Computation: Proving a language non-regular by exhibiting an infinite set of pairwise distinguishable prefixes.

myhill-nerode-classes-and-minimal-automa.meaning: Myhill-Nerode Classes and Minimal Automata: The minimal DFA for a language has exactly one state per Myhill-Nerode equivalence class, so the number of classes is both an achievable design and a proof that no smaller one exists.
myhill-nerode-classes-and-minimal-automa.name: Indistinguishability of prefixes

negative-feedback-gain-desensitization-a.application: Analog Circuits: Every precision analog stage: instrumentation amplifiers, regulators, measurement front ends.
negative-feedback-gain-desensitization-a.meaning: Negative Feedback: Gain Desensitization and Its Price: Feeding a fraction of the output back in opposition trades raw gain for precision: the closed-loop gain stops depending on the amplifier and starts depending on the feedback network.
negative-feedback-gain-desensitization-a.name: Closed-loop gain and desensitization

newton-raphson-quadratic-convergence-and.application: Engineering Mathematics III: Solving nonlinear equations in thermal, structural and circuit problems.
newton-raphson-quadratic-convergence-and.meaning: Newton-Raphson: Quadratic Convergence and Its Failure Modes: One iteration of Newton's method replaces the function by its tangent, and the number of correct digits doubles each step - until the derivative vanishes or the starting point is badly chosen.
newton-raphson-quadratic-convergence-and.name: Newton-Raphson iteration and its local error relation

non-inverting-op-amp-gain.application: Analog Circuits: Sensor conditioning and active filters.
non-inverting-op-amp-gain.meaning: Non-Inverting Op-Amp Gain: With negative feedback and an ideal op amp, the non-inverting closed-loop gain is set by the resistor ratio.
non-inverting-op-amp-gain.name: Non-inverting amplifier gain

nozzle-flow-enthalpy-drop-to-exit-veloci.application: Engineering Thermodynamics: Designing steam and gas turbine nozzle rings, where the enthalpy drop sets the stage velocity triangles.
nozzle-flow-enthalpy-drop-to-exit-veloci.meaning: Nozzle Flow: Enthalpy Drop to Exit Velocity: A nozzle converts enthalpy into kinetic energy, so the exit velocity follows from the enthalpy drop alone - and the speed of sound tells you whether the flow is choked.
nozzle-flow-enthalpy-drop-to-exit-veloci.name: Exit velocity from an enthalpy drop, and the local sonic speed

op-amp-gain-bandwidth-product.application: Analog Circuits: Choosing amplifier stages so the signal band fits inside the closed-loop bandwidth with margin.
op-amp-gain-bandwidth-product.meaning: Op-Amp Gain-Bandwidth Product: An op-amp's open-loop gain rolls off at 20 dB per decade, so gain times bandwidth stays fixed - choose closed-loop gain and the amplifier hands you the matching bandwidth.
op-amp-gain-bandwidth-product.name: Gain-bandwidth product

open-channel-flow-mannings-equation.application: Hydraulics & Hydraulic Machinery: Sizing storm drains, irrigation canals and sewer gravity mains.
open-channel-flow-mannings-equation.meaning: Open-Channel Flow: Manning's Equation: Gravity drives open-channel flow, and Manning's equation ties depth, slope and surface roughness to velocity through the hydraulic radius - the workhorse of drain, canal and sewer design.
open-channel-flow-mannings-equation.name: Manning's equation

orthographic-projection-and-scale.application: Engineering Graphics: Manufacturing drawings and assembly layouts.
orthographic-projection-and-scale.meaning: Orthographic Projection and Scale: Orthographic views use parallel projectors to show true dimensions on faces parallel to the projection plane.
orthographic-projection-and-scale.name: Representative fraction

otto-cycle-compression-ratio-and-efficie.application: Engineering Thermodynamics: Engine calibration decisions: compression ratio versus knock margin versus fuel grade.
otto-cycle-compression-ratio-and-efficie.meaning: Otto Cycle: Compression Ratio and Efficiency: The spark-ignition engine's ideal efficiency is fixed by one geometric number - the compression ratio - raised to a power set by the gas.
otto-cycle-compression-ratio-and-efficie.name: Air-standard Otto efficiency

overall-equipment-effectiveness.application: Production Planning & Control: Finding losses in a production shift.
overall-equipment-effectiveness.meaning: Overall Equipment Effectiveness: OEE combines availability, performance, and quality to describe productive output relative to planned production time.
overall-equipment-effectiveness.name: Overall equipment effectiveness

overall-heat-transfer-coefficient-and-fo.application: Heat Transfer Operations: Selecting exchanger types and finning by matching resistance budgets.
overall-heat-transfer-coefficient-and-fo.meaning: Overall Heat Transfer Coefficient and Fouling: A heat exchanger's duty runs through a stack of resistances - two films, a wall, and the fouling layers time adds - and the weakest resistance's opposite, the lowest h, dominates the total.
overall-heat-transfer-coefficient-and-fo.name: Resistance stack

oxygen-transfer-kla-and-the-fermenter-ox.application: Bioprocess Engineering: Scale-up and fed-batch design where oxygen sets the feed strategy.
oxygen-transfer-kla-and-the-fermenter-ox.meaning: Oxygen Transfer: kLa and the Fermenter Oxygen Balance: Aerobic fermentation is usually oxygen-limited, and the transfer rate from bubble to broth - kLa times the driving force - must meet the culture's uptake or the cells downshift.
oxygen-transfer-kla-and-the-fermenter-ox.name: Oxygen transfer rate

packed-bed-pressure-drop-the-ergun-equat.application: Fluid Flow Operations: Sizing catalyst beds, adsorbers and granular filters against blower or head capacity.
packed-bed-pressure-drop-the-ergun-equat.meaning: Packed-Bed Pressure Drop: The Ergun Equation: Flow through a bed of particles loses head to viscous drag at low speed and to form drag at high speed, and the Ergun equation is the sum of both regimes with the bed's geometry folded in.
packed-bed-pressure-drop-the-ergun-equat.name: Ergun equation

page-replacement-fifo-lru-and-beladys-an.application: Operating Systems: Explaining why real systems approximate LRU (clock algorithm) rather than FIFO.
page-replacement-fifo-lru-and-beladys-an.meaning: Page Replacement: FIFO, LRU and Belady's Anomaly: When every frame is full, the victim-page rule decides the fault count - and FIFO's rule is so naive that adding memory can make it worse.
page-replacement-fifo-lru-and-beladys-an.name: Page fault count

parameterized-queries-and-injection-prev.application: Cryptography & Network Security: Protecting account, billing, and search queries.
parameterized-queries-and-injection-prev.meaning: Parameterized Queries and Injection Prevention: Parameterized database calls keep SQL structure separate from untrusted values so input is interpreted as data, not executable syntax.
parameterized-queries-and-injection-prev.name: Query construction rule

password-storage-salts-and-slow-password.application: Cryptography & Network Security: Protecting account databases if a backup is exposed.
password-storage-salts-and-slow-password.meaning: Password Storage: Salts and Slow Password Hashing: A server stores a salted, deliberately expensive password verifier rather than plaintext or a fast general-purpose hash.
password-storage-salts-and-slow-password.name: Password verifier

pcm-quantization-noise-and-the-6-db-per-.application: Communication Systems: Choosing converter resolution in audio, instrumentation and telecom codecs.
pcm-quantization-noise-and-the-6-db-per-.meaning: PCM Quantization Noise and the 6-dB-per-Bit Rule: Digitizing an analog signal trades noise for bits in a fixed exchange rate: every added quantization bit buys about 6 dB of signal-to-quantization-noise ratio.
pcm-quantization-noise-and-the-6-db-per-.name: SQNR of uniform PCM

pearson-correlation-computation-and-its-.application: Data Science Foundations: Screening many variable pairs before modelling, then verifying with scatter plots.
pearson-correlation-computation-and-its-.meaning: Pearson Correlation: Computation and Its Limits: The correlation coefficient standardizes covariance to [-1, 1] so linear association becomes comparable across datasets - and 'linear' is the word that gets forgotten.
pearson-correlation-computation-and-its-.name: Pearson correlation

pfr-versus-cstr-sizing-for-first-order-r.application: Chemical Reaction Engineering: Choosing reactor type and staging for liquid-phase processing.
pfr-versus-cstr-sizing-for-first-order-r.meaning: PFR versus CSTR Sizing for First-Order Reactions: For the same conversion, a plug-flow reactor is always smaller than a back-mixed one - the CSTR runs entirely at its outlet's slow, low-concentration condition, while the PFR exploits the fast inlet.
pfr-versus-cstr-sizing-for-first-order-r.name: First-order sizing equations

photoelectric-effect-and-work-function.application: Engineering Physics: Photomultipliers and photodiodes that detect light photon by photon.
photoelectric-effect-and-work-function.meaning: Photoelectric Effect and Work Function: Electrons are ejected only when each photon individually carries more energy than the metal's work function; brighter light adds electrons but never energy per electron.
photoelectric-effect-and-work-function.name: Photoelectric energy balance

pipelining-hazards-stalls-and-real-speed.application: Computer Organization & Architecture: Choosing between deeper pipelines (higher clock, more hazard tax) and wider issue.
pipelining-hazards-stalls-and-real-speed.meaning: Pipelining: Hazards, Stalls and Real Speedup: A k-stage pipeline promises k-fold throughput, but data, control and structural hazards tax the promise; the honest speedup divides by the stall cycles actually paid.
pipelining-hazards-stalls-and-real-speed.name: Effective CPI and speedup

plc-sequence-logic-and-safe-interlocks.application: Industrial Automation & PLC Systems: Automating packaging and material-handling cells.
plc-sequence-logic-and-safe-interlocks.meaning: PLC Sequence Logic and Safe Interlocks: A PLC sequence advances machine states only when the required permissives are true and faults or unsafe conditions force a defined safe state.
plc-sequence-logic-and-safe-interlocks.name: Sequence transition rule

poles-zeros-and-stability-in-the-s-plane.application: Signals & Systems: Placing closed-loop poles to meet overshoot and settling specs in control design.
poles-zeros-and-stability-in-the-s-plane.meaning: Poles, Zeros and Stability in the s-Plane: A transfer function's pole locations are the system's natural behaviours: real parts set decay or growth, imaginary parts set oscillation, and the left half-plane is the border of stability.
poles-zeros-and-stability-in-the-s-plane.name: Pole to time-domain mode

position-tolerance-at-maximum-material-c.application: Engineering Drawing & CAD: Tolerancing clearance holes on production drawings where assembly must be guaranteed.
position-tolerance-at-maximum-material-c.meaning: Position Tolerance at Maximum Material Condition: A hole made at its maximum size can be offset further and still assemble, and that bonus tolerance is what makes the maximum-material modifier useful on production drawings.
position-tolerance-at-maximum-material-c.name: Bonus tolerance and the fixed-fastener position tolerance

power-angle-equation-and-transmission-li.application: Power Systems: Setting interconnector transfer limits and series-compensation projects.
power-angle-equation-and-transmission-li.meaning: Power-Angle Equation and Transmission Limits: Real power across a transmission link is a sine of the angle between the two end voltages, and that curve sets both the steady transfer limit and the stability story.
power-angle-equation-and-transmission-li.name: Power-angle relation

power-law-rheology-in-polymer-processing.application: Polymer Science & Processing: Estimating pressure and flow in extrusion dies.
power-law-rheology-in-polymer-processing.meaning: Power-Law Rheology in Polymer Processing: Many polymer melts are shear-thinning; a power-law model relates shear stress to shear rate over a limited processing range.
power-law-rheology-in-polymer-processing.name: Power-law fluid model

precision-recall-and-the-f1-score.application: Machine Learning: Setting alert thresholds where missed positives and false alarms carry different costs.
precision-recall-and-the-f1-score.meaning: Precision, Recall and the F1 Score: Accuracy hides class imbalance; precision and recall expose the two distinct mistakes a classifier can make, and F1 forces a single number to face both.
precision-recall-and-the-f1-score.name: Precision, recall and their harmonic mean

propeller-slip-pitch-and-theoretical-spe.application: Marine Propulsion & Power Systems: Sea-trial analysis and hull-fouling monitoring from routine noon-report data.
propeller-slip-pitch-and-theoretical-spe.meaning: Propeller Slip, Pitch and Theoretical Speed: A propeller is a screw in a fluid that gives way: its theoretical speed comes from pitch times RPM, and the shortfall against actual speed - slip - measures the thrust being made.
propeller-slip-pitch-and-theoretical-spe.name: Propeller slip

psychrometrics-humidity-ratio-and-comfor.application: Refrigeration & Air Conditioning: Coil selection: apparatus dew point and bypass factor set how much moisture a coil removes.
psychrometrics-humidity-ratio-and-comfor.meaning: Psychrometrics: Humidity Ratio and Comfort Cooling: Moist air behaves as a mixture whose water content is tracked by the humidity ratio, and comfort cooling is as much a dehumidification problem as a temperature one.
psychrometrics-humidity-ratio-and-comfor.name: Humidity ratio from vapour pressure

pump-affinity-laws-and-speed-control.application: Hydraulics & Hydraulic Machinery: Evaluating variable-speed drives against throttling and against impeller trimming.
pump-affinity-laws-and-speed-control.meaning: Pump Affinity Laws and Speed Control: Changing a pump's speed moves its whole characteristic: flow in proportion, head with the square and power with the cube - which is why speed control saves energy that throttling wastes.
pump-affinity-laws-and-speed-control.name: Affinity laws for a constant-impeller pump

pump-hydraulic-power-and-head.application: Hydraulics & Hydraulic Machinery: Sizing pumps and estimating energy use.
pump-hydraulic-power-and-head.meaning: Pump Hydraulic Power and Head: Hydraulic power is the rate of potential energy delivered to a fluid flow; shaft input is larger by the inverse of pump efficiency.
pump-hydraulic-power-and-head.name: Hydraulic power

pump-power-npsh-available-and-cavitation.application: Fluid Flow Operations: Selecting pumps for a duty and checking whether the suction arrangement will work.

pump-power-npsh-available-and-cavitation.name: Hydraulic power and available NPSH

pv-array-sizing-peak-sun-hours-and-syste.application: Renewable Energy Systems & Storage: Sizing rooftop, off-grid and mini-grid systems against load profiles.
pv-array-sizing-peak-sun-hours-and-syste.meaning: PV Array Sizing: Peak Sun Hours and System Derates: A PV array's daily energy is its rating times the site's peak sun hours times a stack of loss factors - an arithmetic that sizes arrays, batteries and economics from one irradiation number.
pv-array-sizing-peak-sun-hours-and-syste.name: Daily energy yield

pwm-inverters-modulation-index-and-funda.application: Power Electronics: Motor drives from appliances to traction, where PWM sets both voltage and frequency.
pwm-inverters-modulation-index-and-funda.meaning: PWM Inverters: Modulation Index and Fundamental Control: A PWM inverter chops a DC rail at high frequency, and the ratio of modulating to carrier amplitude - the modulation index - linearly sets the fundamental output voltage.
pwm-inverters-modulation-index-and-funda.name: Fundamental of sinusoidal PWM

quantity-take-off-and-rate-analysis.application: Estimating & Costing: Preparing a bill of quantities.
quantity-take-off-and-rate-analysis.meaning: Quantity Take-Off and Rate Analysis: A measured work item is costed by multiplying its verified quantity by an applicable unit rate, then adding explicit indirect costs and taxes.
quantity-take-off-and-rate-analysis.name: Measured work-item cost

quench-severity-and-section-size-getting.application: Physical Metallurgy & Heat Treatment: Selecting a quench medium for a section size from the cooling rate it must achieve.

quench-severity-and-section-size-getting.meaning: Quench Severity and Section Size: Getting Past the Pearlite Nose: A steel hardens only if its cooling curve reaches the martensite range before the pearlite transformation can start, and section size, quench medium and thermal diffusivity decide whether it does.
quench-severity-and-section-size-getting.name: Newtonian cooling of a section and its time constant

query-cost-selectivity-and-the-index-bre.application: Database Management Systems: Explaining a slow query before adding an index, so the plan and not the intuition drives the decision.
query-cost-selectivity-and-the-index-bre.meaning: Query Cost: Selectivity and the Index Break-Even Point: A planner chooses an index over a table scan when the rows it would fetch are a small enough fraction of the table; that break-even point is a computation you can reproduce.
query-cost-selectivity-and-the-index-bre.name: Cost of an indexed lookup versus a full scan

queueing-headroom-and-replica-sizing.application: Cloud Computing: Setting autoscaling thresholds from a utilisation ceiling rather than a CPU number picked by feel.
queueing-headroom-and-replica-sizing.meaning: Queueing Headroom and Replica Sizing: Capacity is not max throughput divided by per-replica throughput: because waiting time grows without bound as utilisation approaches one, replicas are sized to a utilisation ceiling, not to the peak.
queueing-headroom-and-replica-sizing.name: Utilisation, replica count and Little's law

radial-flow-into-a-well-and-the-log-term.application: Reservoir Engineering: Estimating well productivity and the gain from stimulation or fracture treatment.
radial-flow-into-a-well-and-the-log-term.meaning: Radial Flow into a Well and the Log-Term Insensitivity: Steady radial flow into a well depends only logarithmically on the drainage radius, which is why infill wells add far less production than a linear estimate suggests.
radial-flow-into-a-well-and-the-log-term.name: Steady-state radial inflow into a well

rank-of-a-matrix-and-consistency-of-line.application: Engineering Mathematics I: Deciding whether a structural or circuit model has a unique solution before solving it.
rank-of-a-matrix-and-consistency-of-line.meaning: Rank of a Matrix and Consistency of Linear Systems: A linear system Ax = b has solutions exactly when the coefficient matrix and the augmented matrix have the same rank; the rank then tells you whether the solution is unique or a family.
rank-of-a-matrix-and-consistency-of-line.name: Rouche-Capelli consistency condition

rankine-earth-pressure-and-the-effect-of.application: Soil Mechanics / Geotechnical Engineering: Designing retaining walls, basement walls and bridge abutments.
rankine-earth-pressure-and-the-effect-of.meaning: Rankine Earth Pressure and the Effect of Water Behind a Wall: A retaining wall is designed against the lateral thrust of the soil behind it, and if that soil is saturated the water pressure can exceed the soil's own contribution.
rankine-earth-pressure-and-the-effect-of.name: Rankine active pressure coefficient and resultant thrust

rate-analysis-building-up-a-unit-rate-wi.application: Estimating & Costing: Preparing and checking tender rates against a schedule of rates.
rate-analysis-building-up-a-unit-rate-wi.meaning: Rate Analysis: Building Up a Unit Rate with Overheads and Profit: A tender rate is built from measured quantities, current prices and explicit factors for overheads, profit and waste - and every one of those factors is visible in the arithmetic.
rate-analysis-building-up-a-unit-rate-wi.name: Unit rate from direct cost, overhead and profit

reading-charts-honestly-axes-scales-and-.application: Communication Skills: Reviewing vendor and internal dashboards before acting on a trend.
reading-charts-honestly-axes-scales-and-.meaning: Reading Charts Honestly: Axes, Scales and Visual Distortion: A chart's visual message is the ratio its ink shows; when the axis is truncated or the scale is uneven, that ratio silently exaggerates the data ratio.
reading-charts-honestly-axes-scales-and-.name: Distortion factor

reciprocal-levelling-and-the-curvature-c.application: Surveying: Crossing a river or a ravine where a single setup cannot balance backsight and foresight.
reciprocal-levelling-and-the-curvature-c.meaning: Reciprocal Levelling and the Curvature Correction: Two instrument setups across a river separate the true level difference from the instrument's own collimation error, and the curvature and refraction correction quantifies what the Earth's surface does to a level line.
reciprocal-levelling-and-the-curvature-c.name: Reciprocal levelling and the combined curvature-refraction correction

rectification-average-output-and-ripple.application: Basic Electronics: Front ends of every mains-powered DC supply.
rectification-average-output-and-ripple.meaning: Rectification: Average Output and Ripple: A bridge rectifier folds the negative half-cycles upright, doubling the average output and halving the ripple period compared with a single diode.
rectification-average-output-and-ripple.name: Average output of full-wave rectification (resistive load, ideal diodes)

recurrences-characteristic-roots-and-clo.application: Discrete Mathematics: Analysing divide-and-conquer costs and matrix-power tricks that turn a linear recurrence into logarithmic work.
recurrences-characteristic-roots-and-clo.meaning: Recurrences, Characteristic Roots and Closed Forms: A linear recurrence describes cost, count or state growth; its characteristic roots turn the recursion into a closed form whose dominant root is the growth rate.
recurrences-characteristic-roots-and-clo.name: Solution of a second-order linear recurrence

recycle-bypass-and-purge-balances.application: Process Calculations: Ammonia, methanol and polymerization plants built around per-pass conversion economics.

recycle-bypass-and-purge-balances.meaning: Recycle, Bypass and Purge Balances: Recycle loops make balances iterative on purpose: what leaves unreacted comes back to the reactor, and the steady-state balance closes only when accumulation around the loop is zero.
recycle-bypass-and-purge-balances.name: Recycle balance structure

recycle-overall-conversion-and-the-law-o.application: Process Calculations: Designing reactor-separator loops where per-pass conversion is deliberately kept low.
recycle-overall-conversion-and-the-law-o.meaning: Recycle, Overall Conversion and the Law of Diminishing Returns: A recycle loop raises overall conversion beyond what one pass achieves, but the improvement saturates: each further increment of recycle buys less and costs more circulation.
recycle-overall-conversion-and-the-law-o.name: Overall conversion with recycle of unreacted feed

reduced-voltage-starting-of-induction-mo.application: Electrical Machines II: Starting large motors on a supply with a limited fault level.
reduced-voltage-starting-of-induction-mo.meaning: Reduced-Voltage Starting of Induction Motors: A large induction motor draws several times its rated current at standstill, so starting methods trade current against torque; the trade is a squared ratio that can be computed in advance.
reduced-voltage-starting-of-induction-mo.name: Starting current and torque under reduced voltage

reflection-standing-waves-and-impedance-.application: Electromagnetic Fields: Antenna feed design and the specification of acceptable VSWR for a transmitter.
reflection-standing-waves-and-impedance-.meaning: Reflection, Standing Waves and Impedance Matching: Whenever a guided wave meets an impedance change, part of it reflects back; the reflection coefficient and the standing-wave ratio quantify the mismatch and tell you what matching will buy.
reflection-standing-waves-and-impedance-.name: Reflection coefficient, VSWR and return loss

refrigeration-cop-and-the-condenser-temp.application: Refrigeration & Air Conditioning: Diagnosing efficiency loss from condenser fouling without opening the refrigerant circuit.
refrigeration-cop-and-the-condenser-temp.meaning: Refrigeration COP and the Condenser Temperature Penalty: A vapour-compression cycle's efficiency is bounded by the Carnot limit between its two temperatures, and the condenser temperature costs more than the evaporator temperature is worth.
refrigeration-cop-and-the-condenser-temp.name: Coefficient of performance and its reversible limit

regularization-dropout-and-weight-decay.application: Deep Learning: Standard first-line defense against overfitting in fully connected layers, alongside early stopping.
regularization-dropout-and-weight-decay.meaning: Regularization: Dropout and Weight Decay: Both techniques buy generalization by constraining what the network is allowed to do - dropout by randomly deleting units during training, weight decay by penalizing large weights.
regularization-dropout-and-weight-decay.name: L2-regularized objective and dropout ensemble size

relational-algebra-selection-projection-.application: Database Management Systems: Reading EXPLAIN plans and understanding why a predicate placement changed performance.
relational-algebra-selection-projection-.meaning: Relational Algebra: Selection, Projection and Join: Every SQL query is a relational-algebra expression in disguise, and reading queries as algebra shows what the optimizer is allowed to reorder.
relational-algebra-selection-projection-.name: Query as algebra

relative-volatility-and-minimum-stages-i.application: Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics: Rapid sizing of distillation columns for a proposed separation.
relative-volatility-and-minimum-stages-i.meaning: Relative Volatility and Minimum Stages in Distillation: The ease of a distillation separation is captured by relative volatility, and the minimum number of theoretical stages needed follows from it by a single logarithm.
relative-volatility-and-minimum-stages-i.name: Fenske equation for minimum stages at total reflux

reynolds-number-and-flow-regime.application: Fluid Flow Operations: Estimating pipe friction and pressure loss.
reynolds-number-and-flow-regime.meaning: Reynolds Number and Flow Regime: The Reynolds number compares inertial and viscous effects and helps identify the flow regime in a specified geometry.
reynolds-number-and-flow-regime.name: Pipe Reynolds number

ridge-regularisation-and-numerical-condi.application: Machine Learning: Stabilising models whose features are collinear, where the unregularised solution has enormous coefficient variance.
ridge-regularisation-and-numerical-condi.meaning: Ridge Regularisation and Numerical Conditioning: Adding a squared penalty turns an ill-posed least-squares problem into a well-conditioned one, at the cost of a deliberate, quantifiable shrinkage of the coefficients.
ridge-regularisation-and-numerical-condi.name: Ridge regression solution

routh-hurwitz-stability-criterion.application: Control Systems Engineering: Finding stabilizing controller-gain ranges before simulation.

routh-hurwitz-stability-criterion.meaning: Routh-Hurwitz Stability Criterion: The Routh array counts right-half-plane poles from the characteristic polynomial's coefficients alone - no root solving, and it answers 'for which gains is the system stable?' directly.
routh-hurwitz-stability-criterion.name: Routh stability condition

safe-file-uploads-and-clipboard-trust-bo.application: Cryptography & Network Security: Designing user avatars, homework attachments, or import features.
safe-file-uploads-and-clipboard-trust-bo.meaning: Safe File Uploads and Clipboard Trust Boundaries: Treat uploaded files and pasted clipboard content as hostile input until the server validates and the user explicitly chooses what to do with it.
safe-file-uploads-and-clipboard-trust-bo.name: Upload acceptance gate

safe-input-boundaries-sql-nosql-and-temp.application: Cryptography & Network Security: Reviewing search, filtering, and report endpoints.

volumetric-efficiency-airflow-and-fuel-f.meaning: Volumetric Efficiency, Airflow and Fuel Flow: An engine's power follows its airflow, and airflow is swept volume times density times volumetric efficiency - so boost, speed and breathing are the only levers.

industry.title: Real-world applications

blocks: Power factor correction is a standard commercial practice, and it is usually driven by the tariff rather than by the physics.

Industrial loads are inductive — motors and transformers dominate — so the power factor typically sits around 0.8 lagging. Utilities charge a penalty below about 0.9 or 0.95, because they must size cables, transformers and switchgear on apparent current while billing for real power. Installing a capacitor bank supplies the reactive power locally, removes the penalty, and reduces losses in the site's own distribution.

The sizing is straightforward but the application is not. Overcorrecting makes the power factor leading, which raises the voltage and can be worse than lagging. Capacitors also resonate with system inductance at a particular frequency, and if that is near a harmonic present in the supply the result is amplified distortion and failed capacitors. This is why modern installations use detuned reactors in series with the capacitors, and why a harmonic survey usually precedes the installation.

With variable-speed drives the situation changes again. A drive's rectifier draws current in pulses, so the displacement power factor can be near unity while the true power factor is poor because of harmonics. Correcting with capacitors does nothing here; the fix is an active front end or a line reactor.
The measurement distinction matters: displacement power factor is
at the fundamental, while true power factor includes harmonic distortion. A meter reading one and a tariff specifying the other is a source of genuine billing disputes.

blocks: Activated Sludge: Food-to-Microorganism Ratio is a core model in Environmental Engineering: The aeration tank is a managed microbial ecosystem, and F/M - the daily BOD load per kilogram of biomass - is the dial that sets treatment efficiency, sludge production and oxygen demand. The model is used within these stated limits: Conventional activated sludge operates near F/M 0.2-0.4 /day; extended aeration runs lower (longer sludge age), high-rate systems higher - each with its own efficiency and sludge yield.
advanced.title: Formal definition

blocks: mixed liquor suspended solids, the biomass
Conventional activated sludge operates near F/M 0.2-0.4 /day; extended aeration runs lower (longer sludge age), high-rate systems higher - each with its own efficiency and sludge yield.
advanced.title: Formula and variables

blocks: Microbes eat influent BOD (the food) and grow into more biomass; the operator controls how hard that population is worked by the loading ratio. High F/M means abundant food: fast growth, more waste sludge, looser floc and poorer settling. Low F/M means scarcity: microbes cannibalize their own mass (endogenous respiration), sludge yield drops, settling improves, but tank volume and aeration hours rise. Because MLSS is held by wasting sludge at a chosen age, F/M and sludge age are two views of the same balance - and oxygen demand follows the food actually consumed.
advanced.title: Derivation

blocks: A plant treats 5 MLD at 200 mg/L BOD in a 2,000 m^3 aeration tank holding 2,500 mg/L MLSS. Find F/M.
Convert units and apply the ratio.
Food = 5,000 m^3/day x 0.200 kg/m^3 = 1,000 kg BOD/day. Biomass = 2,000 m^3 x 2.5 kg/m^3 = 5,000 kg MLSS. F/M = 1000/5000 = 0.20 /day.
F/M = 0.20/day - the low end of conventional operation, favouring good settling and nitrification; raising MLSS wasting would push F/M up.

blocks: Active Filters: Cutoff, Quality Factor and the Op-Amp's Bandwidth Bill is a core model in Analog Circuits: A second-order active filter is designed by two numbers - cutoff frequency and quality factor - and both are limited in practice by the amplifier's gain-bandwidth product. The model is used within these stated limits: A unity-gain-buffer or non-inverting Sallen-Key topology with matched resistor and capacitor pairs, an ideal amplifier, and component tolerances ignored. Higher order filters are cascades of such sections.
advanced.title: Formal definition

blocks: quality factor: peaking near the cutoff

A unity-gain-buffer or non-inverting Sallen-Key topology with matched resistor and capacitor pairs, an ideal amplifier, and component tolerances ignored. Higher order filters are cascades of such sections.
advanced.title: Formula and variables

blocks: A second-order section has two poles, placed by its cutoff frequency, and a quality factor that decides how close to the imaginary axis they sit. With matched components the cutoff is set by one resistor-capacitor product, and the quality factor follows from the amplifier gain: unity gain gives Q = 0.5, two real poles and no peaking, while a Butterworth response needs Q = 0.707 and a resonant design needs much higher Q with visible peaking. Quality factor is bought with amplifier gain, and gain is bought with bandwidth from a real op-amp: the loop has to be fast enough to enforce the feedback at the filter's own frequency, so a practical rule is that the amplifier's gain-bandwidth product should exceed the cutoff by two orders of magnitude. This is why a 100 kHz, high-Q filter needs a much faster amplifier than its component values suggest.
advanced.title: Derivation

blocks: A Sallen-Key section uses 10 kilohm resistors and 10 nF capacitors. Find the cutoff frequency and the gain needed for a Butterworth response.
The matched-component cutoff is one over two pi times the resistor-capacitor product; the Butterworth Q fixes the gain.
The resistor-capacitor product is 10^4 x 10^-8 = 10^-4 s, so f_0 = 1/(2 x pi x 10^-4) = 1592 Hz. Butterworth needs Q = 0.707, so 1/(3 - K) = 0.707 gives K = 3 - 1.414 = 1.586.
Cutoff about 1.59 kHz with a gain of 1.586, which is a non-inverting stage with feedback ratio 0.586.
A 10 kHz section with Q = 5 is built with a 1 MHz gain-bandwidth op-amp. Is the amplifier adequate?
Compare the amplifier's gain-bandwidth product with the rule of thumb for the cutoff frequency.
The rule requires about 100 x 10 kHz = 1 MHz, and the chosen amplifier offers exactly 1 MHz.
It is marginal. The measured response will differ from the ideal near the cutoff, and a part with several megahertz of gain-bandwidth is the safer choice.

The model is used within these stated limits: The converter is ideal and its noise floor is below one LSB; the radio dominates the active current; sleep current is constant and the regulator's quiescent loss is included in it.
advanced.title: Formal definition

blocks: Quantisation step, ideal SNR and duty-cycled mean current
duty cycle: fraction of time active
The converter is ideal and its noise floor is below one LSB; the radio dominates the active current; sleep current is constant and the regulator's quiescent loss is included in it.
advanced.title: Formula and variables

blocks: An n-bit converter splits the reference range into two to the n equal steps, so the smallest resolvable change is the reference divided by that count. Quantisation error is uniform over half a step either way, and comparing its power with the power of a full-scale sine gives the well-known six decibels per bit plus 1.76 decibels, which is why resolution is often quoted as a signal-to-noise figure rather than a voltage. On the energy side, a node that is active for a fraction d of the time draws the active current only during that fraction, so the mean current is a convex combination of active and sleep currents; battery life is capacity divided by mean current. The value of the arithmetic is that it shows the two levers: resolution is bought from the converter, and life is bought from the duty cycle, which is why aggressive wake scheduling usually beats a bigger battery.
advanced.title: Derivation

blocks: A 12-bit ADC uses a 3.3 V reference. What is the least significant bit, and what is the ideal signal-to-noise ratio?
Divide the reference by two to the twelfth; apply the six-decibels-per-bit rule.
A step of 0.806 mV and an ideal SNR of 74 dB; a sensor whose noise exceeds a few times that step cannot use the extra bits.
A node draws 25 mA while awake for 2 s every 60 s and 3 microamps asleep. What mean current does it draw, and how long does a 2000 mAh cell last?
Weight the active current by its duty cycle, add the sleep current, then divide capacity by mean current.
d = 2/60 = 0.0333. Active contribution = 25 x 0.0333 = 0.833 mA; plus 0.003 mA sleep gives 0.836 mA. Life = 2000/0.836 = 2392 h.
About 0.84 mA mean and 2392 hours, roughly 100 days of continuous operation from a 2000 mAh cell.

blocks: Adder Carry Chains: Ripple Depth versus Lookahead is a core model in Digital Logic Design: An adder's speed is set by how long its carry takes to cross the word: a ripple chain costs n full-adder delays, and grouping the carry logic turns that into a logarithmic depth. The model is used within these stated limits: Worst-case (carry-propagate) input pattern, static CMOS gates with stated delays, and a single-level grouping. Real libraries add wiring and fan-in limits that stop the depth shrinking indefinitely.
advanced.title: Formal definition

blocks: carry propagation delay of one full adder
delay of one lookahead group level
Worst-case (carry-propagate) input pattern, static CMOS gates with stated delays, and a single-level grouping. Real libraries add wiring and fan-in limits that stop the depth shrinking indefinitely.
advanced.title: Formula and variables

blocks: Each full adder's sum and carry-out depend on its carry-in, so with a ripple chain the carry of bit i must settle before bit i+1 can compute, giving a worst-case path of n delays in series. Carry-lookahead removes the dependency by computing, for each bit, whether it generates a carry or propagates one; a carry into a group is then a function of the group's generate and propagate terms rather than of the previous bit's settle. Because those terms are computed in parallel, the carry depth grows with the logarithm of the number of bits rather than linearly, at the cost of more gates and wider fan-in. The engineering decision is where the log-depth logic stops paying for itself, which is why wide adders use a hierarchy of small lookahead blocks rather than one flat expression.
advanced.title: Derivation

blocks: A 16-bit adder uses full adders with 0.2 ns carry delay. Compare the ripple delay with a lookahead design using 4-bit groups and 0.1 ns per group level.
Ripple is width times per-bit delay; lookahead is one full adder plus log-base-4 of the width group levels.
3.2 ns against 0.4 ns, an eightfold improvement in the adder's critical path, bought with roughly three times the gate area.
A 32-bit ripple adder uses the same 0.2 ns full adder. What is the maximum clock frequency if the adder is the only path in the cycle?
Compute the worst-case delay and take its reciprocal.
Delay = 32 x 0.2 = 6.4 ns, so the period cannot be shorter than 6.4 ns, giving 1/6.4 ns = 156 MHz.
About 156 MHz. A hierarchical lookahead design at roughly 0.2 + 0.1 x 3 = 0.5 ns would allow a period near 0.5 ns, subject to everything else in the path.

blocks: Affine Transformations for Model Manipulation is a core model in CAD / CAM: Moving, scaling and rotating a CAD model is matrix multiplication on every point - and homogeneous coordinates make even translation fit the same multiplication. The model is used within these stated limits: Rigid (rotation+translation) transforms preserve distances; scaling is affine but not rigid, and 3D uses the same 4x4 homogeneous pattern.
advanced.title: Formal definition

blocks: x'\' = cosθ -sinθ\ sinθ cosθ x\ ; translate via 1 0 t_x\\0 1 t_y\\0 0 1
translation offsets carried in the third homogeneous row
Rigid (rotation+translation) transforms preserve distances; scaling is affine but not rigid, and 3D uses the same 4x4 homogeneous pattern.
advanced.title: Formula and variables

blocks: Rotation follows from writing the point in polar form and adding the angle, then expanding with the sine/cosine addition identities - which produces exactly the 2x2 matrix. Translation alone breaks matrix form (it is addition, not multiplication), so homogeneous coordinates append a 1 to points and a row to the matrix, folding translation in. Now every affine operation is one matrix, and sequences compose by multiplying matrices right-to-left: rotate-then-translate differs from translate-then-rotate by exactly the matrix order - the fact that makes assembly constraints and robot kinematics computable.
advanced.title: Derivation

blocks: Rotate the point (10, 0) by 30 degrees counter-clockwise, then translate by (5, 2). Where does it land?
Apply rotation, then translation (in that order).
Rotation: x' = 10 cos30 = 8.66, y' = 10 sin30 = 5. Translation adds (5, 2): (13.66, 7).
(13.66, 7) - and translating first, then rotating, would instead swing the offset too, landing at a different point: order matters because matrices do not commute.

blocks: Air-Fuel Ratio and Combustion Stoichiometry is a core model in Internal Combustion Engines: Complete combustion has an exact chemical recipe; the stoichiometric air-fuel ratio follows from balancing the reaction, and real engines run rich or lean against it deliberately. The model is used within these stated limits: Complete combustion with dry air at 23.2% oxygen by mass; gasoline blends vary around 14.7, diesel stoichiometry is near 14.5 but diesel runs lean overall.
advanced.title: Formal definition

blocks: oxygen moles per mole of octane from balancing C, H and O
actual AFR divided by stoichiometric AFR
Complete combustion with dry air at 23.2% oxygen by mass; gasoline blends vary around 14.7, diesel stoichiometry is near 14.5 but diesel runs lean overall.
advanced.title: Formula and variables

blocks: Balance carbon to CO2, hydrogen to H2O, and count the oxygen the products demand: octane needs 12.5 O2 molecules. Converting to mass - 12.5 x 32 g oxygen per 114 g fuel, divided by oxygen's 23.2% mass share in air - gives about 15.1 kg air per kg fuel for pure octane, with real gasoline quoted near 14.7. Engines then steer around this point: lambda below 1 (rich) for power and cooling, above 1 (lean) for economy, and exactly 1 where the three-way catalyst can clean all three pollutants at once - which is why stoichiometric operation with oxygen-sensor feedback defines petrol emissions control.
advanced.title: Derivation

blocks: An engine burns 4 g/s of gasoline at lambda = 0.9 (rich). Find the air flow and the AFR.
Apply the stoichiometric baseline and lambda.
Stoichiometric air = 4 x 14.7 = 58.8 g/s. At lambda 0.9, actual AFR = 14.7 x 0.9 = 13.23, so air = 4 x 13.23 = 52.9 g/s.
52.9 g/s of air at AFR 13.2 - rich operation, chosen for power or catalyst warm-up, at a fuel-economy penalty.

blocks: Alarm Management: Rates, Priorities and Deadbands is a core model in Industrial Automation & PLC Systems: An alarm is a demand for operator action, and the discipline is arithmetic as much as ergonomics: sustainable rates, distinct priorities, and deadbands that stop chattering signals from consuming both. The model is used within these stated limits: Per-operator normalization; the numbers are industry-consensus targets (ISA-18.2/EEMUA 191), not physics - and bad-actor alarms (chattering, standing) are managed against them by audit.

blocks: Human response is the bottleneck an alarm system must respect: if annunciations outrun the operator's ability to acknowledge, diagnose and act, the display becomes wallpaper exactly when it matters. The rate guidelines convert that intuition into audit numbers; priorities assign each alarm a required response time; deadbands and on/off delays kill the chattering bad actors - a level oscillating across its trip point - that dominate real alarm floods. blocks: A plant logs 900 alarms/day to one operator, 40% of them a single chattering flow transmitter crossing its trip 300 times/day. Assess and fix.
Convert to ISA-style rates and attack the bad actor.

blocks: Amortized Analysis: Dynamic Arrays and the Accounting Method is a core model in Data Structures & Algorithms: A single array append can cost O(n) during a resize, but charged across the whole sequence the average cost per operation stays constant - amortized analysis proves the difference between worst-case-per-op and worst-case-per-sequence. The model is used within these stated limits: Growth by doubling from small capacity; the geometric series of copies sums to less than n, giving the classic tight bound 2n - 1 moves for n appends in the cleanest accounting.
advanced.title: Formal definition

blocks: Amortized bound for n doubling appends
total work of the whole sequence
bound: n writes plus at most n copy-doublings plus slack
Growth by doubling from small capacity; the geometric series of copies sums to less than n, giving the classic tight bound 2n - 1 moves for n appends in the cleanest accounting.
advanced.title: Formula and variables

blocks: Count the sequence, not the step. Appending n items writes n slots directly; resizes copy 1 + 2 + 4 + ... elements, a geometric series that stays below n. The accounting method makes this a bookkeeping rule: charge each append 3 credits - one pays for its own write, one is stored on the element for a future copy, one covers the doubling overhead - so no resize ever finds the array in debt, and the per-operation charge is a constant even though single operations spike.
advanced.title: Derivation

blocks: Starting from capacity 1, append 16 items to a doubling array. Count element moves.
Sum the copy series and add the direct writes.
Copies happen at sizes 1, 2, 4, 8: 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15 element moves. Direct writes: 16. Total 31 moves for 16 appends.
31 total moves, under 2 per append on average - O(1) amortized even though the final resize alone moved 8 elements.
