slope of the equilibrium line, dy/dx

A two-film model with no reaction in the films, dilute solute so that total flow rates are constant, and a linear equilibrium relation over the range of compositions. Reactive absorption needs an enhancement factor.
advanced.title: Formula and variables

blocks: Mass transfer from a gas into a liquid crosses a gas film and a liquid film in series, so the resistances add. The subtlety is the equilibrium relationship between the two phases: a solute much more soluble in the liquid has a shallow equilibrium line, so a small liquid-side resistance corresponds to a large resistance when expressed in gas-side units, and the gas film controls. A sparingly soluble gas such as oxygen has a steep equilibrium line, bringing the liquid film's resistance into the overall figure with a large multiplier. The practical consequence is that the design calculation tells the engineer which film to stir: increasing the gas-side coefficient of a liquid-film-controlled absorber changes almost nothing.
advanced.title: Derivation

blocks: A column has k_G = 0.05 mol/(m^2 s atm) and k_L = 0.02 in matching units, with an equilibrium slope of 1.5. Find the overall gas-phase coefficient.
Multiply the liquid coefficient's reciprocal by the slope, then add and invert.
0.0105 against a gas-film value of 0.05: the liquid film, scaled by the equilibrium slope, controls the rate almost entirely.
For a sparingly soluble gas the equilibrium slope is 0.5 instead. What is the overall coefficient?
Reapply the relation with the new slope.
0.0222: more than double the previous value, because the smaller equilibrium slope gives the liquid film much less weight in gas-side terms.

blocks: Union-Find with Path Compression is a core model in Data Structures & Algorithms: A disjoint-set forest answers 'are these two elements connected?' in effectively constant time by attaching smaller trees under larger ones and flattening every path that a find walks. The model is used within these stated limits: Union by rank or size. The bound is amortised over the operation sequence, not per operation, and path compression may not be combined with a naive union rule.
advanced.title: Formal definition

blocks: Amortised cost of m union-find operations over n elements
inverse Ackermann function, at most 4 for any practical n
Union by rank or size. The bound is amortised over the operation sequence, not per operation, and path compression may not be combined with a naive union rule.
advanced.title: Formula and variables

blocks: Union by rank keeps a tree of rank r holding at least 2^r nodes, so every root has rank at most log2(n) and no find walks more than log2(n) links. Path compression then flattens the links it walks, so a node climbed once is charged a smaller rank class the next time. Each node can be charged to at most alpha(n) rank classes before its rank exceeds the tree size, which gives the O(m alpha(n)) total rather than O(m log n).
advanced.title: Derivation

blocks: Starting from nine singleton sets 1-9, apply union(1,2), union(3,4), union(1,3), then find(4). Trace the parents.
Attach the equal-rank tree under either root and increase that root's rank by one; path compression only happens during a find.

union(1,2): rank 0 and 0, so 2 points to 1 and rank(1)=1. union(3,4): 4 points to 3, rank(3)=1. union(1,3): equal ranks, so 3 points to 1 and rank(1)=2. find(4) walks 4 -> 3 -> 1 and then rewrites both links so 4 and 3 point directly at 1.
Roots are 1 and 5..9. After find(4), parent[4]=1 and parent[3]=1; the tree height below 1 is one link.
Detect the first edge that closes a cycle in an undirected graph with edges a-b, b-c, c-a.
Apply union to each edge; the first edge whose endpoints already share a root closes a cycle.
union(a,b) merges {a,b}. union(b,c) merges {a,b,c}. For c-a: find(c)=a and find(a)=a, the same root, so no merge is performed.
Edge c-a closes the cycle. Processing k edges reports the cycle after O(k alpha(n)) work.

blocks: van 't Hoff Equation and the Equilibrium Constant is a core model in Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics: Temperature moves chemical equilibrium in the direction Le Chatelier described, and van 't Hoff's equation is that principle with numbers: the sign of the reaction enthalpy decides the direction. blocks: Combine the Gibbs-Helmholtz relation for how Delta G/T varies with temperature and Delta G = -RT ln K, and the equilibrium constant's temperature derivative becomes Delta H / RT^2 - heat is the equilibrium's hidden reactant. Integrating at constant Delta H yields the two-point form, structurally identical to Clausius-Clapeyron because boiling is itself an equilibrium. The engineering content: an exothermic synthesis (ammonia, methanol, sulfuric acid's converter stages) pays a falling K at every degree of rise, yet needs heat for rate - the temperature sequence in industrial reactors is a negotiated truce between van 't Hoff and Arrhenius.

blocks: The chain rule expresses an early layer's gradient as a product of every later layer's local derivatives. Sigmoid saturates: its derivative never exceeds 0.25 and approaches 0 in the tails, so each factor is at most a quarter and a five-layer product is at most about 1/1000 - the earliest layers learn glacially. ReLU's positive-side derivative is exactly 1, so depth stops shrinking the signal, at the price of dead units when inputs go negative. Initialization schemes and skip connections attack the same product from the weights side and the topology side.

blocks: Type choice is a correctness decision more often than a performance one, and the mistakes are well documented.
Money is the canonical case. Floating-point cannot represent decimal fractions exactly, so accumulating prices or interest in a

produces rounding errors that show up as a balance off by a cent. Every serious system stores money as an integer count of the smallest unit, or uses a decimal type. This is a recurring source of real financial bugs.

Integer overflow is the other. A 32-bit signed counter overflows at about 2.1 billion, and history includes routers failing after 2^32 seconds of uptime and timestamps breaking in 2038. Languages differ: C and C++ wrap silently on unsigned overflow and invoke undefined behaviour on signed, while Rust panics in debug builds. Knowing what your language does is not optional.

Serialisation and endianness matter at system boundaries. A struct written on a little-endian machine and read on a big-endian one has its bytes reversed, which is why network protocols define byte order explicitly and why formats like Protocol Buffers encode fields with explicit tags rather than relying on memory layout.

blocks: Voltage Drop and Losses on a Distribution Feeder is a core model in Power Systems: Line drop and line loss are two different numbers: the first decides whether customers get the right voltage, the second decides what the utility pays, and both follow from the same current and impedance. The model is used within these stated limits: A short line approximated by series impedance only, balanced load, and a receiving-end referred calculation. Long lines need the full two-port or distributed model, and capacitance matters at higher voltages.
advanced.title: Formal definition

blocks: Per-phase voltage drop and three-phase loss

A short line approximated by series impedance only, balanced load, and a receiving-end referred calculation. Long lines need the full two-port or distributed model, and capacitance matters at higher voltages.
advanced.title: Formula and variables

blocks: A feeder carrying current develops a voltage drop across its series impedance, and only the components of that current in phase with resistance and in quadrature with reactance contribute, which is where the power factor enters. The same current produces a loss proportional to resistance and to the square of current. The exponent in the loss is the reason distribution engineering is obsessed with current reduction rather than resistance reduction: doubling the current quadruples the loss, so reconducting a heavily loaded feeder, moving a transformer closer to the load, or correcting a lagging power factor all attack the same term. The two relations also separate concerns: voltage drop is roughly linear in current and decides the regulated voltage at the far end, while losses are quadratic and decide the annual energy cost.
advanced.title: Derivation

blocks: A feeder carries 100 A at 0.8 power factor with 0.3 ohm resistance and 0.2 ohm reactance per phase. Find the voltage drop and the three-phase loss.
Use the in-phase and quadrature components of current against the line impedance, then the three-phase loss formula.
36 V per phase - about 0.57 % of a 6351 V phase voltage on an 11 kV feeder - and 9 kW of loss that must be supplied continuously.
The same feeder is loaded to 200 A by a new connection. What happens to the loss?
The loss depends on the square of current.
P_loss = 3 x 200^2 x 0.3 = 36,000 W, four times the previous 9 kW.
Loss quadruples to 36 kW for double the current, which is why feeder loading reviews use current squared as the metric.

blocks: Volumetric Efficiency, Airflow and Fuel Flow is a core model in Internal Combustion Engines: An engine's power follows its airflow, and airflow is swept volume times density times volumetric efficiency - so boost, speed and breathing are the only levers. The model is used within these stated limits: Four-stroke cycle with one intake event per two revolutions, naturally aspirated unless a boost pressure is used to set density, and steady-state operation. Volumetric efficiency falls with speed once breathing limits flow.
advanced.title: Formal definition

blocks: Air mass flow and fuel flow for a four-stroke engine

Four-stroke cycle with one intake event per two revolutions, naturally aspirated unless a boost pressure is used to set density, and steady-state operation. Volumetric efficiency falls with speed once breathing limits flow.
advanced.title: Formula and variables

blocks: Every two revolutions a four-stroke engine sweeps its full displacement once, so the ideal air flow is displacement times speed over two. Real engines do less than the ideal because of valve and port restriction, which is what volumetric efficiency accounts for. The mass of air actually inducted follows from the density of that charge, so intake temperature, altitude and boost pressure all act through the same term: this is why turbocharging works, since it raises density without changing displacement or speed. Fuel flow then follows from the target air-fuel ratio, and the arithmetic closes the loop between a power target, an emissions constraint and a fuel system's capacity.
advanced.title: Derivation

blocks: A 2 litre engine runs at 3000 rpm with 90 % volumetric efficiency in air of density 1.184 kg/m^3. Find the air mass flow and the fuel flow at an air-fuel ratio of 14.7.
Convert displacement to cubic metres, apply the flow relation, then divide by the air-fuel ratio.
0.053 kg/s of air and 0.0036 kg/s of fuel, which is 13.0 kg of fuel per hour at this operating point.
The same engine is boosted to an intake density of 1.78 kg/m^3. What air and fuel flows does it see at the same speed and efficiency?
Density enters the airflow relation linearly.
Air flow = 0.9 x 1.78 x 0.002 x 25 = 0.0801 kg/s. Fuel flow at the same ratio = 0.00545 kg/s.
0.080 kg/s of air, 50 % more than naturally aspirated, so a proportional torque increase if the fuel system and combustion limits allow it.

blocks: Every two revolutions a four-stroke engine sweeps its full displacement once, so the ideal air flow is displacement times speed over two. Real engines do less than the ideal because of valve and port restriction, which is what volumetric efficiency accounts for. The mass of air actually inducted follows from the density of that charge, so intake temperature, altitude and boost pressure all act through the same term: this is why turbocharging works, since it raises density without changing displacement or speed. Fuel flow then follows from the target air-fuel ratio, and the arithmetic closes the loop between a power target, an emissions constraint and a fuel system's capacity.
standard.title: Derivation

blocks: A 2 litre engine runs at 3000 rpm with 90 % volumetric efficiency in air of density 1.184 kg/m^3. Find the air mass flow and the fuel flow at an air-fuel ratio of 14.7.
Convert displacement to cubic metres, apply the flow relation, then divide by the air-fuel ratio.
0.053 kg/s of air and 0.0036 kg/s of fuel, which is 13.0 kg of fuel per hour at this operating point.
The same engine is boosted to an intake density of 1.78 kg/m^3. What air and fuel flows does it see at the same speed and efficiency?
Density enters the airflow relation linearly.
Air flow = 0.9 x 1.78 x 0.002 x 25 = 0.0801 kg/s. Fuel flow at the same ratio = 0.00545 kg/s.
0.080 kg/s of air, 50 % more than naturally aspirated, so a proportional torque increase if the fuel system and combustion limits allow it.

Static volumetric estimate before production data exists; B_o converts reservoir barrels (hot, pressurized, gas-dissolved) to stock-tank barrels, and net-pay cutoffs decide h.
advanced.title: Formula and variables

blocks: Multiply down the rock: area times thickness gives gross rock volume; porosity keeps the pore space; water saturation removes the pore volume that water owns; dividing by B_o shrinks the reservoir-condition liquid to what surface separators will measure, because dissolved gas evolves and the oil contracts. What remains is stock-tank oil initially in place - a geological inventory, not a business number. Recoverable reserves multiply the recovery factor, which encodes the displacement physics (sweep efficiency, residual saturation) and the economics; it is why two fields of equal STOIIP can differ tenfold in value, and why enhanced-oil-recovery projects are really RF-improvement projects.
advanced.title: Derivation

blocks: A field spans 1 km^2 with 20 m net pay, porosity 20%, water saturation 30% and B_o = 1.2. Estimate STOIIP and reserves at RF = 30%.
Work the volumetric product, converting units.
Pore volume = 1e6 x 20 x 0.20 = 4e6 m^3. Hydrocarbon pore volume = 4e6 x 0.70 = 2.8e6 m^3. STOIIP = 2.8e6/1.2 = 2.33e6 sm^3 = 2.33e6 x 6.29 = 14.7 MMbbl. Reserves = 14.7 x 0.30 = 4.4 MMbbl.
About 14.7 MMbbl in place, 4.4 MMbbl recoverable at 30% RF - each RF point is worth 147,000 barrels, the leverage of waterflood and EOR decisions.

blocks: Water Activity and Microbial Growth Limits is a core model in Food Process Engineering & Safety: Microbes grow on available water, not total water: water activity - the vapour-pressure ratio - is the number that decides who can grow, and drying, salting and sugaring all attack it. The model is used within these stated limits: Measured at equilibrium and constant temperature; solutes (salt, sugar) and drying lower a_w by binding water, and most pathogens - including C. botulinum below 0.93 - are excluded under ~0.85-0.90.
advanced.title: Formal definition

blocks: a_w=(p)/(p_sat)= ERH/100, growth limits: bacteria 0.90, yeasts 0.87, moulds 0.80
vapour pressure of water in the food
saturation vapour pressure of pure water at the same temperature
equilibrium relative humidity of the headspace
Measured at equilibrium and constant temperature; solutes (salt, sugar) and drying lower a_w by binding water, and most pathogens - including C. botulinum below 0.93 - are excluded under ~0.85-0.90.
advanced.title: Formula and variables

blocks: Microbial cells harvest water by osmosis, which responds to chemical potential - expressed practically as the ratio of the food's water vapour pressure to pure water's. Honey at 17% total moisture may still... actually honey keeps precisely because its sugars bind that moisture to a_w ~ 0.6: moulds cannot grow, bacteria are far excluded. The hierarchy of limits is the preservation map: below 0.90 most bacteria stop, below 0.80 most moulds, below 0.6 nothing grows - so intermediate-moisture foods, cured meats and dried fruit are engineered to a target a_w, and packaging must then hold it against humidity exchange.
advanced.title: Derivation

blocks: A dried fruit is engineered to a_w = 0.70 and packaged. Assess its microbial stability and what the package must guarantee.
Read the number against the growth-limit ladder.

At 0.70 no bacteria or yeasts grow and most moulds are inhibited - shelf-stable against microbes. The package's moisture barrier must keep uptake below the 0.80 mould threshold across the shelf life at worst-case storage humidity.
Microbially stable at 0.70; the engineering risk moves entirely to packaging barrier and humidity excursion - a_w is the spec, moisture content is only its shadow.

standard.title: Formula and variables

blocks: Microbial cells harvest water by osmosis, which responds to chemical potential - expressed practically as the ratio of the food's water vapour pressure to pure water's. Honey at 17% total moisture may still... actually honey keeps precisely because its sugars bind that moisture to a_w ~ 0.6: moulds cannot grow, bacteria are far excluded. The hierarchy of limits is the preservation map: below 0.90 most bacteria stop, below 0.80 most moulds, below 0.6 nothing grows - so intermediate-moisture foods, cured meats and dried fruit are engineered to a target a_w, and packaging must then hold it against humidity exchange.

At 0.70 no bacteria or yeasts grow and most moulds are inhibited - shelf-stable against microbes. The package's moisture barrier must keep uptake below the 0.80 mould threshold across the shelf life at worst-case storage humidity.
Microbially stable at 0.70; the engineering risk moves entirely to packaging barrier and humidity excursion - a_w is the spec, moisture content is only its shadow.

blocks: Water-Cement Ratio and Abram's Law is a core model in Concrete Technology: Concrete strength is governed less by cement brand than by one ratio - water to cement - and Abram's law quantifies the exponential penalty for every extra litre. The model is used within these stated limits: Fully compacted, adequately cured concrete; the excess water evaporates into capillary pores, which is the physical reason strength falls - and durability follows the same pores.
advanced.title: Formal definition

blocks: constants for materials, curing and age; B ~ 10 for classic Abrams data
Fully compacted, adequately cured concrete; the excess water evaporates into capillary pores, which is the physical reason strength falls - and durability follows the same pores.
advanced.title: Formula and variables

blocks: Cement needs roughly w/c ~ 0.25 to hydrate chemically, but workability demands more water; every litre beyond hydration leaves a pore when it evaporates. Strength is the solid's strength diluted by that porosity, and Abrams' experiments collapsed the effect into an exponential law: strength falls by a constant factor per unit increase in w/c. The practical corollaries rule site quality: adding water to a stiff mix at the pump trades away a third of the strength, superplasticizers buy workability without water, and the same pores that cost strength also admit chlorides and freeze-thaw damage - which is why codes cap w/c for exposure severity, not just strength.
advanced.title: Derivation

blocks: Using A/B^(w/c) with B = 10, compare strengths at w/c = 0.4 and 0.6.
Take the ratio of the two exponential terms.
The 0.4 mix is about 58% stronger - one-fifth more water cost more than a third of the strength, the exponential penalty in plain numbers.

blocks: Water Demand Estimation and Population Forecasting is a core model in Environmental Engineering: A water system is sized for a future population, not today's: geometric growth plus per-capita demand sets the design discharge that every downstream unit must carry. The model is used within these stated limits: Geometric growth suits expanding cities; arithmetic or declining-rate methods fit maturing towns - the forecast curve choice alone swings design flows by tens of percent.
advanced.title: Formal definition

blocks: P_{n}=P_{0}(1+r)^{n},\qquad Q=P_{n}\times q\ \text{(plus losses and peak factors)}
P_n=P_0(1+r)^n, Q=P_n× q (plus losses and peak factors)
Geometric growth suits expanding cities; arithmetic or declining-rate methods fit maturing towns - the forecast curve choice alone swings design flows by tens of percent.
advanced.title: Formula and variables

blocks: Populations compound, so the geometric method projects P_0 forward at (1+r)^n - the same relation as compound interest, with r estimated from two or three censuses (or from declining-rate curves for saturating cities). Per-capita demand (135 L/person/day is the Indian norm for Class-I towns) converts people into litres per day, and design practice then layers on losses, industrial demand and peak factors: treatment plant at average-day, distribution mains at peak-hour, which can triple the flow. Every unit downstream - intake, pump, clarifier, filter, reservoir - inherits these numbers.
advanced.title: Derivation

blocks: A town of 100,000 grows at 2.5%/year. Forecast the population after 20 years and the average daily demand at 135 LPCD.
Apply geometric growth, then per-capita demand.
About 164,000 people and 22.1 MLD average demand - the treatment plant's design basis before peak factors and losses are added.

blocks: Welding Heat Input and Joint Integrity is a core model in Manufacturing Processes: Heat input per unit length decides the weld's cooling rate, and cooling rate decides the microstructure, hardness and crack risk of the joint - it is the number procedure specs control. The model is used within these stated limits: Steady manual or mechanized travel; the 60 converts per-second power to per-minute travel units, and plate thickness then sets the cooling rate that matters metallurgically.
advanced.title: Formal definition

blocks: Steady manual or mechanized travel; the 60 converts per-second power to per-minute travel units, and plate thickness then sets the cooling rate that matters metallurgically.
advanced.title: Formula and variables

blocks: The arc delivers V x I watts; the fraction eta that enters the plate spreads along the travel path, so dividing by speed gives energy deposited per millimetre of weld. That number governs everything downstream: high heat input slows cooling, coarsens grains and softens heat-affected zones; low heat input cools fast, risking hard brittle martensite in steels, especially thick ones (which act as their own heat sink). Procedure qualification therefore brackets heat input, and preheat plus interpass temperature manage the cooling rate when thickness or carbon equivalent pushes toward cracking.
advanced.title: Derivation

blocks: An SMAW weld runs at 25 V, 200 A and 250 mm/min with efficiency 0.8. Find the heat input.
About 1.0 kJ/mm - a moderate input typical of structural steel procedures, inside most WPS windows of 0.5-2 kJ/mm.

blocks: Wheatstone Bridge and Null Measurement is a core model in Measurements & Instrumentation: A bridge measures an unknown resistance by balancing two divider ratios to zero output - and null measurement wins because the detector reads zero, not a calibrated scale. The model is used within these stated limits: DC excitation and a sensitive null detector; at balance the result is independent of source voltage and detector calibration, which is the whole point.

blocks: unknown arm solved from the other three
DC excitation and a sensitive null detector; at balance the result is independent of source voltage and detector calibration, which is the whole point.
advanced.title: Formula and variables

blocks: The output is the difference of two divider voltages. When the ratio of one divider matches the other, both midpoints sit at the same potential and the detector sees exactly zero - no current, no loading error, no dependence on how accurate the detector's scale is, only on recognizing null. Solving the ratio equality for the unknown arm gives the classic cross-product. Near balance, the output is approximately linear in small resistance changes, which is how strain-gauge and sensor bridges turn a milliohm shift into a readable millivolt signal.
advanced.title: Derivation

blocks: A bridge balances with R1 = 120 ohm (unknown), R2 = 100 ohm, R3 = 150 ohm, R4 = 125 ohm. Verify balance, then find R1 if R4 were unknown with R1 = 120 known.
Cross-product: 120 x 125 = 15,000 and 100 x 150 = 15,000 - balanced. If instead R4 is unknown with the others fixed: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 = 15000/120 = 125 ohm.
The bridge is balanced; any one arm follows from the other three by the cross-product rule.

blocks: Work Hardening and the Onset of Necking is a core model in Materials Science & Engineering: A ductile metal gets stronger as it is deformed, and the point at which it starts to neck follows from the hardening exponent alone - which is why that exponent is quoted as a design property. The model is used within these stated limits: Isotropic, rate-insensitive work hardening of a metal in uniaxial tension, with the power law fitted over the uniform elongation range. Rate sensitivity and anisotropy need the extended models.
advanced.title: Formal definition

blocks: True stress power law and the Considere condition
Isotropic, rate-insensitive work hardening of a metal in uniaxial tension, with the power law fitted over the uniform elongation range. Rate sensitivity and anisotropy need the extended models.
advanced.title: Formula and variables

blocks: During uniform elongation, straining raises the flow stress by the hardening rate while the cross-section shrinks, so the load carried by the specimen keeps rising until the hardening rate falls to the value of the flow stress. Matching those two quantities is the Considere construction, and it yields the remarkably simple result that instability begins at a true strain equal to the hardening exponent. The same power law gives the true stress at that point. The practical content is that the exponent is not merely a curve-fitting parameter: it sets the uniform elongation of the material, so it decides how much a pressing or forming operation can stretch before the sheet starts to thin locally, which is exactly what formability tests measure.
advanced.title: Derivation

blocks: A steel has K = 600 MPa and n = 0.25. Find the true strain at which necking starts and the true stress there.
Necking starts at a true strain equal to the exponent; substitute into the power law for the stress.
Necking at strain 0.25, so true stress = 600 x 0.25^0.25 = 600 x 0.707 = 424 MPa.
Instability at 25 % true strain and 424 MPa of true stress.
A second steel has n = 0.15 at the same K. Where does it neck, and what does that mean for a stretch-forming operation?
Apply the same condition and compare the resulting strain.
Necking at 0.15 true strain, so the uniform elongation is 60 % of the first material's.
It necks at 15 % strain, so a forming operation that stretches beyond that will thin locally; the first material allows about two thirds more stretch before instability.

blocks: Zener Shunt Regulator: Series Resistor and Dissipation Limits is a core model in Basic Electronics: A shunt regulator holds its output at the breakdown voltage by burning the difference between source and load current, so the design is a two-case calculation: the resistor for minimum input, the zener for maximum input. The model is used within these stated limits: The zener is a shunt element with a voltage/temperature coefficient of its own, the load is resistive or benign, and its current stays within the stated limits. The regulator's efficiency is poor by construction and its output has the zener's noise.
advanced.title: Formal definition

blocks: Series resistor and zener dissipation in a shunt regulator
minimum current that keeps the zener regulating

The zener is a shunt element with a voltage/temperature coefficient of its own, the load is resistive or benign, and its current stays within the stated limits. The regulator's efficiency is poor by construction and its output has the zener's noise.
advanced.title: Formula and variables

blocks: The zener conducts whatever current the load does not take once the series resistor has dropped the input down to the breakdown voltage. Because the input can be low and the load can be high at the same time, the resistor must be small enough to supply the sum of the two worst-case currents; and because the input can be high while the load is minimal, the zener must survive the largest current the resistor can pass. Those two constraints pull in opposite directions, so a shunt regulator is designed at both corners rather than at the nominal operating point. The arithmetic also shows the cost: at no load the entire current allowance is dissipated in the zener, so efficiency and headroom are traded directly against each other.
advanced.title: Derivation

blocks: A 12 V supply varies by 10 % into a 5.1 V zener. Load current ranges from 0 to 20 mA and the zener needs 5 mA to regulate. Choose the series resistor and check the zener's dissipation.
Apply the minimum-input corner for the resistor, then the maximum-input, zero-load corner for the zener power.
220 ohm and a zener rated at 0.5 W or more. The nearest 0.25 W part would be marginal once tolerances and temperature are included.
At the worst-case input with full load, where does the input power go?
Compute the input current and compare the useful output with the losses in the resistor and the zener.
Input current is 36.8 mA, so input power is 13.2 x 0.0368 = 0.486 W. Output power is 5.1 x 0.020 = 0.102 W; the resistor dissipates 0.0368^2 x 220 = 0.298 W and the zener the remaining 0.086 W.
About 21 % efficiency: 0.102 W useful out of 0.486 W in. A shunt regulator trades efficiency for simplicity.

The key relation is Constant P/V impeller-speed rule; check its assumptions before applying it.

explanation: BJT Biasing and the DC Load Line is a core model in Basic Electronics: A transistor amplifier only works where the DC bias parks it, and the load line shows every combination of current and voltage the external circuit permits. The model is used within these stated limits: Active-region operation (V_CE above roughly 0.2-0.3 V); beta varies widely between devices and with temperature, so good bias design must not depend on its exact value. The key relation is Load line and Q-point; check its assumptions before applying it.

body: Zener Shunt Regulator: Series Resistor and Dissipation Limits: A shunt regulator holds its output at the breakdown voltage by burning the difference between source and load current, so the design is a two-case calculation: the resistor for minimum input, the zener for maximum input.

explanation: Blanking Force and Die Clearance is a core model in Manufacturing Processes: Punching a shape out of sheet needs a press whose force covers the whole cut perimeter at once, and a clearance between punch and die set as a fraction of sheet thickness. The model is used within these stated limits: The whole perimeter is sheared simultaneously, the shear strength is taken from the material data sheet, and the press rating must also cover stripping and friction. Clearance values depend on material ductility, with harder sheet needing slightly more. The key relation is Blanking force and die clearance; check its assumptions before applying it.

body: Welding Heat Input and Joint Integrity: Heat input per unit length decides the weld's cooling rate, and cooling rate decides the microstructure, hardness and crack risk of the joint - it is the number procedure specs control.

explanation: Blasting Design: Powder Factor, Burden and Fragmentation is a core model in Mine Planning & Operations: A production blast is engineered rock-breaking: burden and spacing set the broken volume per hole, and the powder factor prices the energy that fragments it. The model is used within these stated limits: Hard-rock bench blasting with a single free face; subdrilling, stemming and decking refine the basic pattern, and PF is compared across sites at equal energy, not equal mass. The key relation is Broken volume and powder factor; check its assumptions before applying it.

body: Stripping Ratio and Open-Pit Mine Planning: Stripping ratio compares waste removed with ore recovered and is one input to an economic open-pit limit.

The model is used within these stated limits: Standard 5-day, 20-degree-C dark incubation; strong wastes must be diluted so some oxygen survives, and the seed microbes must be acclimated. The key relation is Diluted BOD test; check its assumptions before applying it.

explanation: Bolted Joints: Preload and Load Sharing is a core model in Machine Design: A properly preloaded bolted joint makes the clamped members absorb most of the external load - the bolt only feels the stiffness fraction, and the joint never separates. The model is used within these stated limits: Joint remains in compression (F_ext below the separation load F_i/(1-C)); bolt and members act as springs in series-parallel around the load path. The key relation is Joint stiffness factor and bolt load; check its assumptions before applying it.

body: Fatigue: Endurance Limit and the Goodman Line: Cyclic loads fail parts far below yield; the endurance limit bounds infinite life for fully reversed stress, and the Goodman line extends that bound to mean-stress reality.

explanation: Boolean algebra manipulates binary variables with AND, OR and NOT under a set of identities. A Karnaugh map is a graphical arrangement of minterms in Gray-code order that allows adjacency-based minimisation of sum-of-products or product-of-sums expressions. The key relation is Boolean identities and grouping rules; check its assumptions before applying it.

body: Logic Families: Noise Margin and Fan-Out: Two voltage windows and two current budgets decide whether one gate's output can be another gate's reliable input - noise margin for voltage, fan-out for current.
options.label: A

body: Counters: Ripple versus Synchronous and Modulus Design: A counter is flip-flops plus steering logic; ripple counters pay delay per stage while synchronous counters pay it once - and the modulus decides how many stages are needed.

options.label: C

body: Simplifying logic expressions so circuits need fewer gates - the manual version of what synthesis tools automate.

explanation: Boost Converter Design: Duty, Inductor Ripple and Output Ripple is a core model in Power Electronics: A boost converter's duty ratio sets its voltage ratio, its inductor sets the current ripple and its capacitor sets the output ripple - three numbers that can be chosen independently. The model is used within these stated limits: Continuous conduction mode with an ideal switch and diode, negligible equivalent series resistance, and a steady-state duty ratio. Parasitic elements and the diode drop reduce the achievable ratio. The key relation is Boost conversion relations; check its assumptions before applying it.

body: Boost Converter Design: Duty, Inductor Ripple and Output Ripple: A boost converter's duty ratio sets its voltage ratio, its inductor sets the current ripple and its capacitor sets the output ripple - three numbers that can be chosen independently.

options.label: C

body: PWM Inverters: Modulation Index and Fundamental Control: A PWM inverter chops a DC rail at high frequency, and the ratio of modulating to carrier amplitude - the modulation index - linearly sets the fundamental output voltage.
options.label: D

explanation: Brake Thermal Efficiency of an Engine is a core model in Internal Combustion Engines: Brake thermal efficiency compares useful shaft power with the chemical energy rate entering in the fuel. The model is used within these stated limits: Use consistent power and energy units and specify whether the fuel heating value is LHV or HHV. The key relation is Brake thermal efficiency; check its assumptions before applying it.

explanation: Buffers and the Henderson-Hasselbalch Equation is a core model in Engineering Chemistry: A buffer resists pH change because it contains both members of an acid-base pair, and the ratio of their concentrations sets where it holds. The model is used within these stated limits: A weak acid and its conjugate base in dilute aqueous solution at a temperature near 25 degrees C, with concentrations well above the dissociation constant so the equilibrium approximations hold. Ionic strength shifts pKa slightly. The key relation is Henderson-Hasselbalch relation and buffer response; check its assumptions before applying it.

explanation: Cache Headers, ETags and Conditional Requests is a core model in Web Technologies: HTTP caching is a freshness contract: max-age says how long a copy stays usable silently, and validators let a stale copy be reconfirmed cheaply instead of refetched. The model is used within these stated limits: Applies to cacheable methods and statuses; private data needs Cache-Control: private or no-store, and weak versus strong ETags decide whether byte-identity is promised. The key relation is Freshness and revalidation; check its assumptions before applying it.

explanation: Cache is small, fast memory between the CPU and main memory that exploits temporal locality (recently used data will be used again) and spatial locality (nearby data will be used soon). Access is organised in fixed-size cache lines, typically 64 bytes. The key relation is Average memory access time; check its assumptions before applying it.

body: The CPU Performance Equation and Amdahl's Law: Program time is instructions times cycles-per-instruction divided by clock rate, and Amdahl's law caps what speeding up any one part can do for the whole.

body: Miss Rates and Average Memory Access Time Across Cache Levels: Memory performance is a sum of expected penalties: each level's miss rate multiplies the cost of the level beneath it, so a small improvement where misses are frequent beats a large one where they are rare.

explanation: CAD/CAM: From Parametric Model to Verified Toolpath is a core model in CAD / CAM: A parametric CAD model expresses design intent; CAM transforms a checked part model and setup into a machine-specific toolpath. The model is used within these stated limits: RSS assumes independent, suitably distributed contributions; worst-case stack-up instead sums absolute limits. The key relation is Tolerance stack-up for independent dimensions; check its assumptions before applying it.

body: Toolpath Step-Over, Scallop Height and Machining Time: A CAM toolpath is a set of trades: feed rate buys cycle time, step-over buys surface finish, and the cusp left between passes can be predicted before the part is cut.

The model is used within these stated limits: The reference must be valid and non-zero; uncertainty and traceability should accompany a reported result. The model is used within these stated limits: Use the same time window and define whether curtailment and outages are included; capacity factor is not conversion efficiency. The key relation is Capacity factor; check its assumptions before applying it.

explanation: Capacity Requirements from Demand, Work Content and OEE is a core model in Production Planning & Control: Capacity planning is arithmetic on three numbers: how much work a part needs, how many parts are wanted, and what fraction of the available time the equipment is actually productive. The model is used within these stated limits: One product or a stable mix, planned time excluding breaks and planned maintenance, and an OEE measured rather than assumed. Mixed models need the work content weighted by mix, and shared equipment needs a load profile by period. The key relation is Effective capacity and machine requirement; check its assumptions before applying it.

body: Little's Law: WIP, Throughput and Lead Time: In any steady flow system, work in process equals throughput times lead time - no assumptions about routing, variability or process detail, which is why the law is a management lever.

explanation: Carnot Efficiency and the Reversible Limit is a core model in Engineering Thermodynamics: No engine between two temperatures can beat the Carnot fraction, so the second law hands every heat engine a ceiling computed from temperatures alone. The model is used within these stated limits: Temperatures must be absolute; the bound applies to engines exchanging heat with two reservoirs, and real engines fall below it through irreversibilities. The key relation is Carnot efficiency; check its assumptions before applying it.

explanation: Equivalent Standard Axles and Pavement Load Accumulation is a core model in Transportation Engineering: Pavement damage grows roughly with the fourth power of axle load, so one heavy vehicle can be worth thousands of cars and the design traffic is counted in equivalent standard axles. The model is used within these stated limits: The fourth-power law is an empirical damage equivalence derived from road tests on a particular set of pavements and axle configurations; tyre pressure, suspension and climate all shift the real damage, and single, tandem and tridem axles use different reference loads. The key relation is Equivalent standard axles and cumulative traffic; check its assumptions before applying it.

explanation: Error-Budget Burn Rate and Two-Window Alerting is a core model in Site Reliability Engineering: A burn rate expresses how fast an error budget is being spent, which turns an SLO into an alerting rule: a short window catches fast burns, a longer window catches slow ones. The model is used within these stated limits: Errors are countable at the service boundary, traffic is roughly stationary across the window, and the SLO is expressed as a fraction of requests. explanation: Eutectic Reactions and Reading Phase Diagrams is a core model in Materials Science & Engineering: A phase diagram is a map of stable phases versus temperature and composition, and the eutectic point is its most important landmark: the lowest-melting composition, where one liquid freezes into two solids at once. The model is used within these stated limits: Binary systems with limited solid solubility; at the eutectic, three phases coexist so the reaction runs at constant temperature until one phase is consumed - the halt on a cooling curve. The key relation is Eutectic invariant reaction; check its assumptions before applying it.

The key relation is Kirchhoff's current and voltage laws; check its assumptions before applying it.

explanation: Leakage Currents and the Safety Limit That Decides Circuit Values is a core model in Biomedical Instrumentation & Devices: Patient safety in medical electronics is quantified in microamps: the current that can flow through a patient at mains frequency is set by capacitance and voltage, and it constrains isolation design directly. The model is used within these stated limits: Sinusoidal voltage across a purely capacitive path, which is the conservative model for a mains-frequency leakage measurement. Real paths include resistive components from insulation and contamination, and the standard's limits vary with the applied part type. The key relation is Capacitive leakage current through an isolation barrier; check its assumptions before applying it.

explanation: Limit State Design: Partial Safety Factors is a core model in Design of Reinforced Concrete Structures: Limit-state design separates what might happen (factored loads) from what material actually delivers (divided strengths), so a single inequality guarantees a target reliability. explanation: Log-Mean Temperature Difference and Exchanger Duty is a core model in Heat & Mass Transfer: A heat exchanger's duty is its overall conductance times area times a mean temperature difference, and the logarithmic mean is the number that correctly averages the two ends of the exchanger. Multi-pass and cross-flow arrangements need a correction factor multiplying the log-mean value. The key relation is Log-mean temperature difference and duty; check its assumptions before applying it.

The model is used within these stated limits: DC specifications at rated supply and temperature; both margins must be positive, and mixing families requires checking every one of the four voltage numbers, not just the supply. The key relation is Noise margins and fan-out; check its assumptions before applying it.

The key relation is Loom production rate; check its assumptions before applying it.
